'''Alexander Allen Silvestro''' (born November 15, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-source-ravens-met-with-tight-end-alex-silvestro-20121106,0,7759501.story |title=Ravens sign tight end Alex Silvestro to practice squad, cut Dennis Dixon |author=Wilson, Aaron |date=November 7, 2012 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |access-date=November 10, 2012 |archive-date=July 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130722063638/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-source-ravens-met-with-tight-end-alex-silvestro-20121106,0,7759501.story |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Prior to Rutgers, Silvestro played for [[Paulsboro High School]] in [[Paulsboro, New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Chappelear |first=Scott |title=Paulsboro High School product Alex Silvestro helping Patriots prepare for Super Bowl |work=[[Gloucester County Times]] |publisher=Frank Gargano |date=February 2, 2012 |url=http://www.nj.com/gloucester-sports/index.ssf/2012/02/paulsboro_high_school_product_1.html |access-date=February 5, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Reiss |first=Mike |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/boston/new-england-patriots/post/_/id/4723809/leftovers-from-bill-belichick-7 |title=Leftovers from Bill Belichick - New England Patriots Blog - ESPN Boston |date=13 June 2012 |publisher=Espn.go.com |access-date=2012-06-23}}</ref>

==Professional career==
[[File:Alex Silvestro.jpg|thumb|Alex Silvestro]]

===New England Patriots===
As a [[defensive end]], he was signed by the [[New England Patriots]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2011. On February 4, 2012, he was called up to replace a former college teammate, [[Tiquan Underwood]], on the active roster of the [[New England Patriots]], one day before [[Super Bowl XLVI]], though he didn't appear in the game.<ref>Shpigel, Ben. [https://www.nytimes.com/2017/11/22/sports/football/one-nfl-game.html "One Game to Remember. Just One.These six men are members of an exclusive group: They played only one N.F.L. game. They are proud of the distinction — and sometimes haunted by it. "], ''[[The New York Times]]'', November 22, 2017. Accessed November 22, 2017. "In a move perceived as coldhearted from the outside but as standard operating procedure from those within the sport, the Patriots released receiver Tiquan Underwood. Replacing him on the active roster was Silvestro, Underwood’s former teammate at Rutgers.... Despite being active, Silvestro came close to entering only once, when Rob Ninkovich missed a play. Silvestro, Ninkovich’s backup, grabbed his helmet, but when New England switched the defensive front, he was told not to rotate in."</ref> During the 2012 OTAs and minicamp, Silvestro was forced into duty at [[tight end]] due to a shortage at that position of the roster.

===Baltimore Ravens===
In November 2012, he was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] to the practice squad. On August 30, 2013, he was released by the Ravens.<ref>{{cite web | title=Ravens make first batch of cuts ahead of roster deadline | work=baltimoresun.com | url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-ravens-cutting-inside-linebacker-nigel-carr-20130830,0,2802036.story | access-date=August 30, 2013 | archive-date=October 4, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004215626/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bal-ravens-cutting-inside-linebacker-nigel-carr-20130830,0,2802036.story | url-status=dead }}</ref>

'''Alex Ronald Bayer''' (born November 8, 1990) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former [[tight end]]. He is currently the [[special teams]] coordinator at [[Syracuse Orange Football|Syracuse University]]. He was signed by the Rams as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2014. He played [[college football]] for the [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green Falcons]].

==Early life==
Bayer had six school records at [[Pickerington High School North]], including 50 receptions for 625 yards and two touchdowns his senior season, where he earned honorable mention all-state and also earned first-team All-OCC and first-team all-central district. Ohio Magazine ranked him the 60th ranked recruit and third-best tight end from the state of [[Ohio]], while [[ESPN.com]] ranked him as one of the top-75 tight ends in the nation.

==College career==
Bayer played in all 12 games, making four starts, during his redshirt freshman season. He was named to [[Phil Steele]]’s All-Freshman Team (Fifth Team) after recording 22 catches for 298 yards and one touchdown on the season. Played in and started all 12 games in 2011 and had 20 receptions for 242 yards and two touchdowns on the year. He finished 2012 with 36 receptions for 410 yards and three touchdowns. He was named to John Mackey Mid-Season Watch List and was named Third-team All-MAC. During his senior season, Bayer played in and started all 14 games, catching 37 passes for 593 yards and 4 touchdowns. Was named third-team All-MAC as a tight end and played in the [[East-West Shrine Game]] in [[St. Petersburg, Florida]], following the season.

==Professional career==

=== St. Louis Rams ===
Bayer was signed by the [[St. Louis Rams]] after going undrafted in [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played in six games during the 2014 season, recording one fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BayeAl00.htm|title=Alex Bayer Stats - Pro-Football-Reference.com|author=|date=|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=April 8, 2017}}</ref> On September 5, 2015, Bayer was released from the St. Louis Rams.<ref>{{Cite web|author=|date=September 5, 2015|title = 2015 St. Louis Rams: Here's Who Didn't Make the 53-Man Roster In The Latest Round Of Cuts|url = http://www.turfshowtimes.com/2015/9/5/9267489/2015-st-louis-rams-official-53-man-roster-cuts|website = Turf Show Times|access-date = December 11, 2015}}</ref>

=== San Diego Chargers ===
On September 6, 2015, the San Diego Chargers signed Bayer to their practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web|date=September 6, 2015|title = Chargers add TE Alex Bayer to practice squad|url = http://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2015/9/6/9271063/san-diego-chargers-sign-tight-end-alex-bayer-practice-squad|website = Bolts From The Blue|access-date = December 11, 2015}}</ref> On December 9, 2015, Bayer was placed on PS-Injured Reserved and eventually cut ending his short lived NFL career.<ref>{{Cite web|date = December 9, 2015|title = Adrian Phillips Waived Among Trio of Roster Moves|url = http://www.chargers.com/news/2015/12/09/adrian-phillips-waived-among-trio-roster-moves|website = San Diego Chargers|access-date = December 11, 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151212013015/http://www.chargers.com/news/2015/12/09/adrian-phillips-waived-among-trio-roster-moves|archive-date = December 12, 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref>

==Coaching career==

===Otterbein===
Following his playing career, Bayer joined the [[Otterbein Cardinals football]] staff as a graduate assistant coaching the tight ends for the 2017 and 2018 seasons. He graduated in April 2019 with his Master's degree in teaching.<ref name="WF">{{cite web |title=Alex Bayer |url=https://godeacs.com/sports/football/roster/coaches/alex-bayer/642 |website=godeacs.com |publisher=University of Wake Forest SID |access-date=January 13, 2022}}</ref>

===Wake Forest===
After his graduation from Otterbein, Bayer reunited with his college coach, [[Dave Clawson]]. Bayer joined the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest]] staff as a special teams analyst, working closely with the Deac's special teams coordinator and tight ends coach, [[Wayne Lineburg]].<ref name="WF" />

===Valparaiso===
Bayer spent the 2021 season as the special teams coordinator at [[Valparaiso Crusaders football|Valparaiso]]. His special teams led the nation in blocked kicks, with nine.<ref name="BG">{{cite news |last1=Briedis |first1=Vincent |title=Loeffler Names Alex Bayer Special Teams Coordinator |url=https://bgsufalcons.com/news/2022/1/13/football-loeffler-names-alex-bayer-special-teams-coordinator.aspx |access-date=January 13, 2022 |work=bgsufalcons.com |publisher=Bowling Green State University SID |date=January 13, 2022}}</ref>

===Bowling Green===
In January 2022, Bayer returned to his alma mater, [[Bowling Green Falcons football|Bowling Green]], after being hired by [[Scot Loeffler]] as the Falcons' special teams coordinator.<ref name="BG" />

===Syracuse===

On January 21, 2026, Bayer joined Coach [[Fran Brown]] as the special teams coordinator for [[Syracuse Orange Football|Syracuse University]]. <ref name="SU">{{cite news |title=Bayer named Special Teams Coordinator |url=https://cuse.com/news/2026/1/21/bayer-named-special-teams-coordinator |work=cuse.com |access-date=January 21, 2026}}</ref>

'''Alex Collins''' (August 26, 1994 – August 13, 2023), was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks football|Arkansas Razorbacks]] and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the fifth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]] with the 171st overall pick. He spent two seasons with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in 2017 and 2018 before re-signing by Seattle in 2020. He played one season with the [[Memphis Showboats (2022)|Memphis Showboats]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL).

==Early life==
[[File:Semper Fidelis All-American Bowl East team practice, Day 1 130104-M-EK802-362 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|alt=Alex Collins, a running back with the east coast team of the Semper Fidelis All-American Bowl, attempts to spot a hole in the defensive line during the team's first practice on December 31, 2012.|Collins in high school in 2012]]

Alex Collins was born on August 26, 1994, in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00.htm |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He attended [[South Plantation High School]] in Fort Lauderdale where he was a [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[high school football|football]], [[basketball]], [[lacrosse]], and [[track and field|track]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Omar |date=April 12, 2016 |title=Former South Plantation standout Alex Collins is on the Dolphins' radar |url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/sfl-former-south-plantation-standout-alex-collins-is-on-the-dolphins-radar-20160412-story.html |access-date=February 7, 2018 |website=Sun-Sentinel.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kasinitz |first=Aaron |date=July 26, 2018 |title='We all knew': Baltimore Ravens' Alex Collins has long envisioned this opportunity – can he seize it? |url=https://www.pennlive.com/baltimore-ravens/2018/07/we_all_knew_baltimore_ravens_a.html |access-date=December 14, 2022 |website=pennlive |language=en}}</ref> He was named Broward County Player of the Year as a junior after rushing for 1,786 yards and 28 [[touchdown]]s as the Paladins earned seven victories and qualified for the state playoffs. As a senior, he rushed for 1,400 yards and 14 touchdowns despite missing three games due to injury, helping South Plantation to nine wins, the district title and a berth in the 8A state playoffs. Following his senior season, he was selected to play in the Semper Fidelis [[All-American]] Bowl, where he was teammates with fellow Arkansas signee [[Austin Allen (quarterback)|Austin Allen]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Tyler |date=June 13, 2018 |title=NFL Razorbacks: Austin Allen carries family name to Tampa Bay |url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Arkansas-Razorbacks-quarterback-Austin-Allen-NFL-Tampa-Bay-Buccaneers-Brandon-Allen-Los-Angeles-Rams-football-119007652/ |access-date=December 4, 2018 |website=HawgSports.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

Also a talented [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]], Collins ran the third leg on South Plantation's state-champion [[4 × 100 metres relay|4 × 100 m relay]] (41.98 s), leading to him being named the 2013 Broward County Male Athlete of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins |url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/alex-collins-2587 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160509141933/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/alex-collins-2587 |archive-date=May 9, 2016 |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=TrackingFootball.com}}</ref>

Collins was ranked as a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]] and the 13th best [[running back]] in his class.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins, 2013 Running Back |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2013/alex-collins-14162 |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Collins committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Arkansas]] in February 2013.

On signing day, Collins's mother provided some momentary drama, when she refused to sign the [[National Letter of Intent]] (LOI) for him to attend school at Arkansas, and then ran away with the LOI. She wanted Collins to stay close to home and attend the [[University of Miami]]. The drama ended the next day when Arkansas head coach [[Bret Bielema]] faxed another LOI to Collins, which was signed by his father.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kurtenbach |first=Dieter |date=February 4, 2013 |title=Hurricanes miss on five-star running back, as Alex Collins commits to Arkansas |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-02-04/sports/sfl-alex-collins-commits-to-arkansas-20130204_1_bret-bielema-alex-collins-charlie-partridge |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610145245/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-02-04/sports/sfl-alex-collins-commits-to-arkansas-20130204_1_bret-bielema-alex-collins-charlie-partridge |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=Sun-Sentinel.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gorten |first=Steve |date=February 7, 2013 |title=Finally: South Plantation star running back signs with Arkansas |url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-02-07/sports/sfl-alex-collins-to-nbc6-im-staying-with-arkansas-20130206_1_alex-collins-razorbacks-friendship-with-arkansas-assistant |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610145350/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2013-02-07/sports/sfl-alex-collins-to-nbc6-im-staying-with-arkansas-20130206_1_alex-collins-razorbacks-friendship-with-arkansas-assistant |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=Sun-Sentinel.com}}</ref>

==College career==

2016 |website=ArkansasNews.com}}</ref>

In his sophomore season in [[2014 Arkansas Razorbacks football team|2014]], Collins ran for 1,100 yards and 12 touchdowns on 204 carries, while still splitting time with Williams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-collins-1/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He also helped lead Arkansas to a [[2014 Texas Bowl|Texas Bowl]] victory over the [[2014 Texas Longhorns football team|Texas Longhorns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas Bowl – Arkansas vs Texas Box Score, December 29, 2014 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2014-12-29-texas.html |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Williams went down with an injury before the 2015 season, so Collins became the featured back in Bret Bielema's offense. He started every game his junior year, and on November 7, 2015, with 108 yards against [[2015 Ole Miss Rebels football team|Ole Miss]], Collins became only the third player in SEC history to rush for 1,000 plus yards in three seasons, joining [[Herschel Walker]] and [[Darren McFadden]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arkansas at Mississippi Box Score, November 7, 2015 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2015-11-07-mississippi.html |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Collins finished his junior season with a career-high 1,577 yards, and a school-record 20 rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-collins-1/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was named second-team all-SEC, mostly because [[2015 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]]'s [[Derrick Henry]] and [[2015 LSU Tigers football team|LSU]]'s [[Leonard Fournette]] outrushed him and were All-Americans. Collins led Arkansas to a [[2016 Liberty Bowl (January)|Liberty Bowl victory]] over [[2015 Kansas State Wildcats football team|Kansas State]] on January 2, 2016. He finished the 45–23 victory with 185 yards and three rushing touchdowns, earning MVP honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liberty Bowl – Kansas State vs Arkansas Box Score, January 2, 2016 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2016-01-02-arkansas.html |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Collins is second on the Razorback career rushing yards list (3,703), behind only Darren McFadden (4,590).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arkansas Razorbacks Rushing |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/arkansas/rushing.html |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On January 10, 2016, Collins penned an open letter to Arkansas fans announcing his intention to forgo his senior season and enter the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalland |first=Robby |date=January 10, 2016 |title=Arkansas star RB Alex Collins declares for 2016 NFL Draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/arkansas-star-rb-alex-collins-declares-for-2016-nfl-draft/ |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=cbssports.com}}</ref> He was projected to be third round pick and was ranked the third best running back by [[CBS Sports|CBSSports.com]] prior to the combine.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zorn |first=Alex |date=November 15, 2015 |title=Why Alex Collins deserves to climb up NFL Draft boards |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/arkansas-football/alex-collins-is-draft-gold/ |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=Saturdaydownsouth.com}}</ref> He attended the [[NFL Combine]] and completed nearly all of the required drills, but chose to not perform the [[short shuttle]] or [[three-cone drill]] due to a headache. His combine performance was described as underwhelming and mediocre. On March 16, 2016, Collins opted to participate at Arkansas's [[pro day]] along with teammates [[Hunter Henry]], [[Brandon Allen (American football)|Brandon Allen]], [[Jonathan Williams (running back, born 1994)|Jonathan Williams]], [[Denver Kirkland]], [[Mitchell Loewen]], [[Sebastian Tretola]], and five others. He performed positional drills and added four inches to his [[vertical jump|vertical]], finishing with a 32½.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2016 |title=11 Arkansas Razorbacks at Arkansas Pro Day 2016 |url=http://www.nwahomepage.com/razorback-nation/11-former-razorbacks-at-arkansas-pro-day-2016/401611675 |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=NwaHomepage.com}}</ref> On April 12, 2016, it was reported that Collins had a pre-draft visit with representatives from the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Omar |date=April 12, 2016 |title=Former South Plantation standout Alex Collins is on the Dolphins' radar |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/sfl-former-south-plantation-standout-alex-collins-is-on-the-dolphins-radar-20160412-story,amp.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201131331/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-dolphins/sfl-former-south-plantation-standout-alex-collins-is-on-the-dolphins-radar-20160412-story,amp.html |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=sun-sentinel.com}}</ref> At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, Collins was projected to be a third or fourth round pick by the majority of [[NFL draft]] experts and analysts. He was ranked the fifth best running back in the draft by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' and [[Pro Football Focus]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 26, 2016 |title=Final 2016 PFF Draft Board: Top 250 NFL prospects |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/draft-final-2016-pff-draft-board-top-250-nfl-prospects |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref> Collins was also ranked the tenth best running back by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=*Alex Collins, DS #10 RB, Arkansas |url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=126869&draftyear=2016&genpos=RB |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=nfldraftscout.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Burke |first=Chris |date=April 12, 2016 |title=2016 NFL draft position rankings |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/04/12/nfl-draft-2016-position-rankings-players-prospects |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=si.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
====2016====
The [[Seattle Seahawks]] selected Collins in the fifth round (171st overall) of the 2016 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kelly |first=Danny |date=April 30, 2016 |title=NFL Draft Results: Seahawks select Alex Collins with 5th round pick, 171 overall |url=http://www.fieldgulls.com/2016/4/30/11494486/nfl-draft-results-seahawks-select-alex-collins-with-5th-round-pick |access-date=May 6, 2016 |website=FieldGulls.com |publisher=SBNation}}</ref> He was the 13th running back selected in the 2016 NFL Draft and one of three running backs the Seahawks drafted in 2016, along with [[C. J. Prosise]] (third round, 90th overall) and [[Zac Brooks]] (seventh round, 247th overall). His former teammate and backup at Arkansas, [[Jonathan Williams (running back, born 1994)|Jonathan Williams]], was selected before him by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the fifth round (156th overall).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/draft.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 6, 2016, Collins signed a four-year deal worth $2.2 million overall with a $184,000 bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=May 6, 2016 |title=Reports: Seahawks' first-round pick Germain Ifedi, four others, agree to contract terms |url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/reports-seahawks-first-round-pick-germain-ifedi-four-others-agree-to-contract-terms |access-date=May 23, 2016 |website=seattletimes.com |publisher=Seattle Times}}</ref>

Upon arriving at the Seahawks' [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]], Collins began competing with [[Thomas Rawls]], [[Christine Michael]], Prosise, Brooks, and [[Troymaine Pope]] for the role as the starting running back after it was left vacant by the retirement of [[Marshawn Lynch]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=August 31, 2016 |title=Seahawks-Raiders What to Watch: Alex Collins, C.J. Prosise, Trevone Boykin and more |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-raiders-what-to-watch-alex-collins-c-j-prosise-trevone-boykin-and-more/ |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=seattletimes.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cohen |first=Stephen |date=May 7, 2016 |title=Seahawks' rookie running backs embracing competition |url=https://www.seattlepi.com/sports/football/amp/Seahawks-rookie-minicamp-Prosise-Collins-Brooks-7420806.php |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=seattlepi.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Farrar |first=Doug |date=June 2, 2016 |title=Marshawn Lynch's replacements: A look at Seattle's current RB situation |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/06/02/seattle-seahawks-running-backs-replacing-marshawn-lynch |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=SI.com}}</ref> Collins had an impressive training camp and was given a chance to showcase his abilities after Rawls missed the starts of training camp while still recovering from injury and Prosise missed a stretch of camp with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boling |first=Dave |date=August 3, 2016 |title=Dave Boling: Rookies already get what it takes to be Seahawks |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/dave-boling/article93546762.html |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=thenewstribune.com}}</ref> After a mediocre preseason, head coach [[Pete Carroll]] named Collins the fourth running back on the Seahawks' depth chart behind Michael, Rawls, and Prosise.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bradley |first=Logan |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Michael listed as starting RB over Rawls on Seahawks depth chart |url=https://www.fansided.com/2016/09/06/christine-michael-listed-starting-rb-seahawks-depth-chart/ |access-date=November 28, 2017 |website=FanSided}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Seahawks' Week 2 matchup against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], but had no gain on two carries in their 9–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Los Angeles Rams – September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180ram.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The next week, Collins had 12 rushing yards on four carries and made the first two [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] of his career for 19 receiving yards in a 37–18 victory over the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. He caught his first career pass from [[Russell Wilson]] and gained nine-yards in the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks – September 25th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250sea.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On October 16, 2016, Collins had a nine-yard reception and one carry for a two-yard gain and the first touchdown of his career during Seattle's 26–24 defeat over the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at Seattle Seahawks – October 16th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610160sea.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Collins finished his rookie season with 31 carries for 125 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown, in 11 games. He also caught 11 passes for 84 receiving yards. Collins also had eight carries for rushing 27 yards and three receptions for 28 receiving yards in two playoff games.<ref name="stats16">{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

After a 10–5–1 season, the Seahawks finished atop the [[NFC West]] and received a playoff berth.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Seattle Seahawks Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sea/2016.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On January 7, 2017, Collins had six carries for 13 rushing yards and one 11-yard reception in the Seahawks' 26–6 victory over the [[Detroit Lions]] in the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#NFC: Seattle Seahawks 26, Detroit Lions 6|Wild Card Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Detroit Lions at Seattle Seahawks – January 7th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701070sea.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> They lost the following game to the Falcons by a score of 36–20 in the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#NFC: Atlanta Falcons 36, Seattle Seahawks 20|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Seattle Seahawks at Atlanta Falcons – January 14th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701140atl.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2017====
Collins competed with Rawls, [[Eddie Lacy]], [[Chris Carson]], [[Mike Davis (running back)|Mike Davis]], Prosise, and [[J. D. McKissic]] throughout training camp for the job as starting running back.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=July 27, 2017 |title=Most Interesting Seahawks Training Camp Storylines: No. 2, Who Carries The Load In A Competitive Backfield?' |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/07/27/most-interesting-seahawks-training-camp-storylines-no-2-who-carries-load-competitive |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180320140212/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/07/27/most-interesting-seahawks-training-camp-storylines-no-2-who-carries-load-competitive |archive-date=March 20, 2018 |access-date=November 29, 2017 |website=seahawks.com}}</ref> On August 30, 2017, it was reported that the Seahawks were fielding trade offers for Collins and cornerback [[Jeremy Lane]]. The Seahawks had no role for Collins after Lacy, Rawls, and Prosise were slated to have the bulk of the carries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 31, 2017 |title=Report: Seahawks gauging trade market for Jeremy Lane, Alex Collins |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/31/report-seahawks-gauging-trade-market-for-jeremy-lane-alex-collins/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171204032354/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/08/31/report-seahawks-gauging-trade-market-for-jeremy-lane-alex-collins/ |archive-date=December 4, 2017 |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Collins was waived by the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drovetto |first=Tony |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Seahawks Make Three More Trades, Set 53-Man Roster |url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/09/02/seahawks-make-three-more-trades-set-53-man-roster |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009153425/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/09/02/seahawks-make-three-more-trades-set-53-man-roster |archive-date=October 9, 2017 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
====2017====
On September 5, 2017, Collins was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. The Ravens signed Collins and former [[Chicago Bears]] running back [[Jeremy Langford]] to provide depth after [[Kenneth Dixon (American football)|Kenneth Dixon]] tore his [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] in training camp.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=September 5, 2017 |title=Ravens Complete Practice Squad With Four Signings |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Complete-Practice-Squad-With-Four-Signings/6c567ff9-42fd-4ed7-9891-f7f04d9d27fa |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115213837/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Complete-Practice-Squad-With-Four-Signings/6c567ff9-42fd-4ed7-9891-f7f04d9d27fa |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

On September 16, 2017, Collins was promoted to the active roster after [[Danny Woodhead]]
was injured in the season-opener and was estimated to miss four-to-six weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=September 16, 2017 |title=Ravens Swap Running Backs and Cornerbacks Ahead of Sunday's Game |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Swap-Running-Backs-and-Cornerbacks-Ahead-of-Sundays-Game/faa6fc83-db1f-4ef0-9051-e5c089e05f3a |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180122043307/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Swap-Running-Backs-and-Cornerbacks-Ahead-of-Sundays-Game/faa6fc83-db1f-4ef0-9051-e5c089e05f3a |archive-date=January 22, 2018 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> Head coach [[John Harbaugh]] named him the Ravens' third running back on the depth chart, behind [[Terrance West]] and [[Javorius Allen]]. The following day, Collins made his Ravens debut and had seven carries for 42 rushing yards and one fumble in the 24–10 victory over the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Baltimore Ravens – September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170rav.htm |access-date=October 28, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> On October 10, 2017, Collins earned his first career start against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and finished the 26–9 loss with nine carries for 82 rushing yards and a fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens – October 1st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710010rav.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 8 matchup against the [[Miami Dolphins]] on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', he rushed for a career high of 113 yards on 18 carries and also caught two passes for 30 yards in the Ravens' 40–0 victory. Although Woodhead returned in Week 9, Collins remained the starting running back and maintained his carries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barber |first=Kyle |date=November 4, 2017 |title=Danny Woodhead's return should not interfere with Alex Collins' carries |url=https://www.baltimorebeatdown.com/2017/11/1/16592596/danny-woodheads-return-should-not-interfere-with-alex-collins-carries-ravens-runningbacks-fantasy |access-date=November 29, 2017 |website=BaltimoreBeatdown.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Miami Dolphins at Baltimore Ravens – October 26th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710260rav.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On November 19, 2017, Collins made his fifth consecutive start and rushed for 49 yards on 20 carries while also scoring his first rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter of a 23–0 defeat over the [[Green Bay Packers]]. He had seven consecutive games without a fumble after analysts criticized him for fumbling twice in three games and worried about his ball security moving forward.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Edward |date=November 26, 2017 |title=Ravens' Alex Collins said his first touchdown of 2017 'felt long overdue |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bs-sp-ravens-alex-collins-happy-to-get-first-touchdown-of-2017-story,amp.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201131659/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/ravens-insider/bs-sp-ravens-alex-collins-happy-to-get-first-touchdown-of-2017-story,amp.html |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |access-date=November 29, 2017 |website=BaltimoreSun.com}}</ref> On November 27, 2017, he had 16 carries for 60 rushing yards and scored an eight-yard touchdown run in a 23–16 win against the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at Baltimore Ravens – November 27th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711270rav.htm |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The following week, Collins had 75 rushing yards and 23 receiving yards to go along with a career-high two touchdowns in a 44–20 win over the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Baltimore Ravens – December 3rd, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712030rav.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the next game, on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'' against the Steelers, he ran the ball 18 times for 120 yards and a touchdown, as well as catching two passes for 46 yards, helping the Ravens total 152 yards on the ground. Despite what was arguably the best game of his career so far, the Steelers narrowly escaped with a win in the 39–38 shootout.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers – December 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712100pit.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Collins led the Ravens in rushing yards for the 2017 season with 973 yards, along with six rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Baltimore Ravens Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/rav/2017.htm |access-date=February 8, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2018====
Collins entered the 2018 season slated as the Ravens starting running back. He started 10 games, recording 411 rushing yards and seven touchdowns along with 15 receptions for 105 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 1, 2018, with a foot injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Clifton |date=December 1, 2018 |title=Kenneth Dixon Activated From Injured Reserve, Alex Collins Placed on IR |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/press-release-ravens-activate-rb-kenneth-dixon |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105220422/https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/press-release-ravens-activate-rb-kenneth-dixon |archive-date=January 5, 2023 |access-date=October 16, 2022 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

====2019====
On March 1, 2019, Collins was waived by the Ravens after he was arrested following a car crash that morning.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=March 1, 2019 |title=Ravens waive RB Alex Collins following arrest |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ravens-waive-rb-alex-collins-following-arrest-0ap3000001019852 |access-date=November 18, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 3, 2019, he pleaded guilty to possession of more than 10 grams of [[marijuana]] and possession of a handgun in a vehicle and received a sentence of 18 months of unsupervised probation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruiz |first=Nathan |date=October 4, 2019 |title=Former Ravens RB Alex Collins pleads guilty to two misdemeanors, to serve 18 months of unsupervised probation |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/ravens/bs-sp-ravens-alex-collins-20191004-5q66xhq7fvfexfrexj2uvrtw6y-story.html |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=BaltimoreSun.com}}</ref> He was suspended three weeks by the NFL on November 1, 2019, for violating the league's personal conduct policy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hagemann |first=Andie |date=November 1, 2019 |title=Free-agent RB Alex Collins suspended 3 games for arrest |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/free-agent-rb-alex-collins-suspended-3-games-for-arrest-0ap3000001071932#2ndlevel |access-date=November 3, 2019 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was reinstated from suspension on November 19, 2019.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1196928511094722562 |user=RapSheet |title=From the transaction wire: Free agent RB Alex Collins is no longer suspended and eligible to sign. He's also healthy from a broken leg and can work out for teams. |date=November 19, 2019}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On November 4, 2020, Collins was signed to the Seahawks' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=November 4, 2020 |title=Seahawks Sign Alex Collins & Mychal Kendricks To Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-alex-collins-mychal-kendricks-to-practice-squad |access-date=October 16, 2022 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster on November 7, 2020, November 14, 2020, and January 2, 2021, for the team's weeks 9, 10, and 17 games against the Bills, Rams, and 49ers, and reverted to the practice squad after each game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=November 7, 2020 |title=Seahawks Activate DE Rasheem Green, Elevate Two From Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-activate-de-rasheem-green-elevate-two-from-practice-squad |access-date=December 13, 2020 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rauschenberg |first=Nathan |date=November 14, 2020 |title=Time For "Snacks," Carson & Hyde Ruled Out And Other Roster Moves For Sunday vs. Rams |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/time-for-snacks-carson-hyde-ruled-out-and-other-roster-moves-for-sunday-vs-rams |access-date=December 23, 2020 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=January 2, 2021 |title=Seahawks Activate CB Tre Flowers From IR; Two Placed On Reserve/COVID-19 List |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-activate-cb-tre-flowers-from-ir-two-placed-on-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=February 15, 2021 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He scored a touchdown against the Rams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at Los Angeles Rams – November 15th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011150ram.htm |access-date=November 18, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Against the 49ers, he ran the ball for 29 yards on five carries, including a game-sealing eight-yard touchdown run with less than two minutes left.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers – January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030sfo.htm |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was elevated again for the team's Wild Card Round game against the Rams, and reverted to the practice squad again following the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=January 8, 2021 |title=Alex Collins Elevated From Practice Squad For Seahawks' Wild Card Game vs. Rams |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/alex-collins-elevated-from-practice-squad-for-seahawks-wild-card-game-vs-rams |access-date=February 16, 2021 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> His practice squad contract with the team expired after the season on January 18, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Five no longer under contract |url=https://www.fantasyguru.com/seahawks-five-no-longer-under-contract/ |access-date=February 18, 2021 |website=FantasyGuru.com |archive-date=March 5, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305154259/https://www.fantasyguru.com/seahawks-five-no-longer-under-contract/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Collins re-signed with the team on February 24, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=February 24, 2021 |title=Seahawks re-sign Alex Collins |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/02/24/seahawks-re-sign-alex-collins/ |access-date=February 24, 2021 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref> In the 2021 season, Collins finished with 108 carries for 411 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go along with nine receptions for 87 receiving yards. He started six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Collins 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CollAl00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=October 17, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Memphis Showboats===
On January 14, 2023, Collins signed with the [[Memphis Showboats (2022)|Memphis Showboats]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL).<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1614305467249065985 |user=USFLShowboats |title=Free Agent Signing |date=January 14, 2023 |access-date=January 17, 2023}}</ref> On April 29, 2023, in a game against the [[Houston Gamblers (2022)|Houston Gamblers]], he threw a touchdown pass.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1652474043419820033 |user=USFLShowboats |title=ARE YOU KIDDING ME?! Did I just witness @Budda03 throw a TOUCHDOWN?! |date=April 29, 2023 |access-date=May 5, 2023}}</ref> Collins was placed on the team's injured reserve list on May 4.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1654293778050744320 |user=USFLShowboats |title=Transferred Player to Injured Reserve List |date=May 4, 2023 |access-date=May 5, 2023}}</ref>

== Death ==
Collins was killed in a traffic collision in [[Lauderdale Lakes, Florida]], on the evening of August 13, 2023, when the [[motorcycle]] that he was riding crashed into the rear passenger side of an [[SUV]] at high speed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=de la Fuente |first=Homero |date=August 15, 2023 |title=Former NFL player Alex Collins dies in motorcycle accident at age 28 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/08/15/sport/alex-collins-nfl-death-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=August 15, 2023 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref> He was pronounced dead at the scene, and it was later reported that he likely died instantly.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 14, 2023 |title=Former Seahawks, Ravens RB Alex Collins dies in Lauderdale Lakes crash |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/miami/news/former-seahawks-ravens-rb-alex-collins-dies-in-crash/ |access-date=August 15, 2023 |website=[[CBS Miami]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=August 14, 2023 |title=Former Seahawks, Ravens RB Alex Collins dead at 28 |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/former-seahawks-ravens-rb-alex-collins-dead-at-28 |access-date=August 14, 2023 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

'''Alexander Rhys Carter''' (born October 19, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the third round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]].

==Early life==
Carter attended [[Briar Woods High School]] in [[Ashburn, Virginia]], where he recorded over 1,000 [[all-purpose yards]] and 50 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] with five [[interceptions]] (one returned for [[touchdown]]) as a senior. He helped lead his team to a 12–1 record and a win in the state championship game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.loudoun.k12.va.us/site/default.aspx?PageType=3&ModuleInstanceID=85338&ViewID=7b97f7ed-8e5e-4120-848f-a8b4987d588f&RenderLoc=0&FlexDataID=100074&PageID=78334 |title=Briar Woods makes almost-perfect run to 2nd state football title |access-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231193717/http://www.loudoun.k12.va.us/site/default.aspx?PageType=3&ModuleInstanceID=85338&ViewID=7b97f7ed-8e5e-4120-848f-a8b4987d588f&RenderLoc=0&FlexDataID=100074&PageID=78334 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was named Virginia's 2011 [[Gatorade Player of the Year]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1305214 |title=Carter named Gatorade Player of the Year |access-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-date=October 7, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007035136/https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1305214 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was selected to play in the 2012 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.loudoun.daily-monitor.com/briar-woods%E2%80%99-carter-selected-for-army-all-american-bowl-2/8758/ |title=Briar Woods' Carter Selected for Army All-American Bowl |access-date=December 31, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231203306/http://www.loudoun.daily-monitor.com/briar-woods%E2%80%99-carter-selected-for-army-all-american-bowl-2/8758/ |archive-date=December 31, 2014 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

Carter also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in [[track & field]] at Briar Woods, competing during his junior year running the 100 meters, 4x100 and the long jump (6.62m or 21-7). He competed at the state meets and his fastest time in the [[100-meter dash]] was 10.9 seconds.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208065390 |title=Carter is Coming Along - GoStanford.com |access-date=February 23, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223160821/http://www.gostanford.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30600&ATCLID=208065390 |archive-date=February 23, 2015 }}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Carter was ranked as the third-best [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] prospect of his class, and drew comparisons to [[Tyvon Branch]].<ref>[https://rivals.yahoo.com/stanford/football/recruiting/player-Alex-Carter-114209 Alex Carter - Yahoo Sports]</ref> On April 5, 2011, he accepted a scholarship offer and announced his commitment to [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]].<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/recruiting-insider/post/briar-woods-wrdb-alex-carter-commits-to-stanford/2011/04/05/AFGFbhjC_blog.html Briar Woods WR/DB Alex Carter commits to Stanford]</ref>

==College career==
As a true freshman in 2012, Carter played in all 14 games with starts in the last 8 games at [[cornerback]].<ref>[http://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/Alex-Carter-Stanford-s-freshman-starter-3985500.php Alex Carter Stanford's freshman starter]</ref> He recorded 46 tackles, including three [[tackles for loss]], and led his team with three forced [[fumbles]]. In 2013, he started all 13 games, recording 59 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss, one interception, team-high seven [[pass breakups]]. In 2014, he started all 13 games, recording 41 tackles with one interception and a team leading nine pass breakups.

On December 31, 2014, he announced he would forgo his remaining eligibility and enter the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>[https://www.nfl.com/news/stanford-cb-alex-carter-decides-to-enter-2015-nfl-draft-0ap3000000452303 Stanford CB Alex Carter decides to enter 2015 NFL Draft]</ref><ref>[http://www.stanforddaily.com/2014/12/31/alex-carter-declares-for-2015-nfl-draft/ Alex Carter declares for 2015 NFL Draft]</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
Carter was selected 80th overall by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref name="draftpick">{{cite web| url = http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Detroit-Lions-trade-up-draft-cornerback-Alex-Carter/041ea319-69eb-4c75-bb4f-eb1a1f67b235 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304105730/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-insider/article-1/Detroit-Lions-trade-up-draft-cornerback-Alex-Carter/041ea319-69eb-4c75-bb4f-eb1a1f67b235 | url-status = dead | archive-date = March 4, 2016 | title = Detroit Lions trade up, draft cornerback Alex Carter | publisher = [[Detroit Lions]] | first = Tim | last = Twentyman | date = May 1, 2015 | access-date = May 1, 2015 }}</ref> The Lions traded up with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] for the pick, giving away their own third-round pick (88th overall, Vikings picked [[Danielle Hunter]]) and their fifth-round pick (143rd overall, Vikings picked [[MyCole Pruitt]]).<ref name="draftpick"/>

On September 3, 2016, Carter was waived by the Lions and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions establish 53-man roster|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/436b48fc-7f92-4d4a-8c0f-05664a3afe93|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 3, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015012008/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/436b48fc-7f92-4d4a-8c0f-05664a3afe93|archive-date=October 15, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign 8 players to team's practice squad|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/article-1/Lions-sign-8-players-to-teams-practice-squad/27beee34-e776-466f-99c9-1afb7f807aef|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 4, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015012030/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/article-1/Lions-sign-8-players-to-teams-practice-squad/27beee34-e776-466f-99c9-1afb7f807aef|archive-date=October 15, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 24, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions sign CB Alex Carter to active roster from practice squad|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-CB-Alex-Carter-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad/623a3785-5786-4a12-81ae-937517bb8410|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227014740/http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-sign-CB-Alex-Carter-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad/623a3785-5786-4a12-81ae-937517bb8410|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 27, 2016|website=DetroitLions.com|date=December 24, 2016}}</ref>

Carter was converted to safety during the 2017 offseason. He was waived by the Lions on September 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions establish 53-man roster|url=http://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac|website=DetroitLions.com|date=September 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903005052/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/news-short/article-1/Lions-establish-53-man-roster/afd5f964-b8d1-4f20-8b0b-055acb8905ac|archive-date=September 3, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 9, 2017, Carter was signed to the [[New England Patriots]]' practice squad, but was released three days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots make changes to the practice squad|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/10/09/patriots-make-changes-practice-squad|website=Patriots.com|date=October 9, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180113072122/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/10/09/patriots-make-changes-practice-squad|archive-date=January 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots make changes to the practice squad|url=http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/10/12/patriots-make-changes-practice-squad|website=Patriots.com|date=October 12, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180117210900/http://www.patriots.com/news/2017/10/12/patriots-make-changes-practice-squad|archive-date=January 17, 2018}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
On November 14, 2017, Carter was signed to the [[Seattle Seahawks]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/11/14/seahawks-make-roster-moves|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=November 14, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180117224118/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/11/14/seahawks-make-roster-moves|archive-date=January 17, 2018}}</ref> He was released on November 21, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Waive Defensive End Dwight Freeney|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/11/21/seahawks-waive-defensive-end-dwight-freeney|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=November 21, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202015338/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/11/21/seahawks-waive-defensive-end-dwight-freeney|archive-date=February 2, 2018}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On November 27, 2017, Carter was signed to the [[Chicago Bears]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | last=Eurich | first=Matt | title=Alex Carter signed to Bears practice squad | website=247Sports | date=2017-11-27 | url=https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/article/alex-carter-signed-to-chicago-bears-practice-squad-111245506/ | access-date=2026-03-21}}</ref> He was released on December 12, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears Sign LB Jonathan Anderson & DL Caushaud Lyons To Practice Squad|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/bears-sign-lb-jonathan-anderson-dl-caushaud-lyons-practice-squad/|date=December 12, 2017}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On December 19, 2017, Carter was signed to the Seahawks' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Waive LB Kache Palacio|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/12/19/seahawks-waive-lb-kache-palacio|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=December 19, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180124032700/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/12/19/seahawks-waive-lb-kache-palacio|archive-date=January 24, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Seahawks on January 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign Six To 2018 Future Contracts|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2018/01/02/seahawks-sign-six-2018-future-contracts|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=January 2, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108003547/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2018/01/02/seahawks-sign-six-2018-future-contracts|archive-date=January 8, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on August 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Sign CB Jeremy Boykins & LB Josh Forrest; Waive S Alex Carter & TE Je'Ron Hamm|url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-cb-jeremy-boykins-lb-josh-forrest-waive-s-alex-carter-te-je-ron-ha|author=Boyle, John|website=Seahawks.com|date=August 2, 2018}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On August 12, 2018, Carter signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign defensive back Alex Carter|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-defensive-back-alex-carter|website=Panthers.com|date=August 12, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on August 31, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers announce first wave of cuts|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-announce-first-wave-of-cuts|author=Henson, Max|website=Panthers.com|date=August 31, 2018}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On December 18, 2018, Carter was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 18, 2018 |title=Redskins Sign Harlan Miller, Place Joshua Holsey On Injured Reserve |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-harlan-miller-place-joshua-holsey-on-injured-reserve |access-date=March 29, 2026 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 27, 2018.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 27, 2018 |title=Redskins Sign Marcus Smith And Alex Carter, Place Colt McCoy And Jordan Reed On Injured Reserve |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-marcus-smith-and-alex-carter-place-colt-mccoy-and-jordan-reed-on-i |access-date=March 29, 2026 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>
He was waived on April 30, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 30, 2019 |title=Redskins Sign Eight College Free Agents |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/redskins-sign-eight-college-free-agents |access-date=March 29, 2026 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Has two children, Mikah Alexander Carter (born February 15, 2018) with ex-wife Ariana Alston, and Akani Christian Carter (born October 28, 2021) with former girlfriend Akasha Marie. Carter's father, [[Tom Carter (American football)|Tom]], was a first-round draft pick in the [[1993 NFL draft]] by the [[Washington Redskins]].

'''Alex Reed Singleton''' (born December 7, 1993) is a Canadian-American<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=2023-03-21 |title=Mile High Morning: ILB Alex Singleton reflects on CFL career at Flames game |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/mile-high-morning-ilb-alex-singleton-reflects-on-cfl-career-at-flames-game |access-date=2026-05-21 |website=Denver Broncos }}</ref> professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Montana State Bobcats football|Montana State Bobcats]] and was signed as an undrafted [[free agent]] by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] after the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He has also played for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==College career==
He played [[college football]] for the [[Montana State Bobcats football|Montana State Bobcats]].

===Seattle Seahawks===
Singleton was signed as an undrafted rookie free agent by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on May 8, 2015.  He signed a three-year contract worth $1,578,500 and received a $3,500 signing bonus.  On September 5, he was released.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Singleton Contract Details |url=http://overthecap.com/player/alex-singleton/4507/ |access-date=January 5, 2016 |website=overthecap.com |publisher=Over The Cap}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
Three days later, Singleton was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kyed |first=Doug |date=September 8, 2015 |title=Patriots Sign Ex-Seahawks Linebacker Alex Singleton To Practice Squad |url=http://nesn.com/2015/09/patriots-sign-ex-seahawks-linebacker-alex-singleton-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=January 5, 2016 |website=nesn.com |publisher=New England Sports Network}}</ref>  He was released on September 15, 2015.

===Minnesota Vikings===
Singleton was signed to the [[Minnesota Vikings]]' practice squad on December 22, 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gates |first=Christopher |date=December 22, 2015 |title=Minnesota Vikings Sign Alex Singleton To Practice Squad |url=http://www.dailynorseman.com/2015/12/22/10647574/minnesota-vikings-sign-alex-singleton-to-practice-squad |access-date=January 5, 2016 |website=dailynorseman.com |publisher=Daily Norseman}}</ref> He was released on April 13, 2016.

===Calgary Stampeders===
Singleton was selected by the [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) with the sixth overall pick in the [[2016 CFL draft]]. He had acquired a Canadian passport in October 2015, having qualified for dual citizenship because his mother was born in [[Toronto]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-01-07 |title=Singleton reportedly joining NFL's Eagles after release from Stampeders |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/cfl/alex-singleton-stampeders-release-cfl-1.4968802 |website=CBC.ca}}</ref> Under then-recently implemented CFL rules, Singleton's Canadian citizenship automatically qualified him to be counted as a Canadian "national" player – previously, players who did not play a meaningful part of their amateur football careers in Canada were counted as "international" players even if they were Canadian citizens. Singleton signed with the team on May 17, 2016. He made his CFL debut on June 25, 2016, against the [[BC Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ALEX SINGLETON |url=http://www.stampeders.com/players/alex-singleton/608786/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704013111/http://www.stampeders.com/players/alex-singleton/608786/ |archive-date=July 4, 2016 |access-date=July 3, 2016 |publisher=stampeders.com}}</ref>

Singleton had an exceptional first season in the CFL and quickly became one of the Stampeders important players on defense.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 21, 2016 |title=Landry: Stamps' rookie Singleton making it look easy |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2016/10/21/landry-stamps-singleton-rolling-rookie-season/ |access-date=January 10, 2017 |website=CFL.ca}}</ref> Over the course of the season, he played in all 18 regular season games, and the Stamps two playoff games. He contributed 65 defensive [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 9 [[special teams]] tackles, and 3 forced [[fumbles]].

On November 1, 2017, Singleton was announced as the team's nominee for the [[CFL's most outstanding defensive player]], [[most outstanding Canadian]] and [[CFL's Most Outstanding Player Award|most outstanding player]] awards, including sweeping all votes in the defensive and Canadian player categories. His 121 tackles going into week 20 of the CFL season were already the most in Calgary Stampeders history.<ref>{{cite news |last=Busby |first=Ian |date=November 1, 2017 |title=Singleton snags triple honours for Stamps – 3DownNation |work=3DownNation |url=http://3downnation.com/2017/11/01/singleton-snags-triple-honours-stamps/ |url-status=dead |access-date=November 1, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107005251/http://3downnation.com/2017/11/01/singleton-snags-triple-honours-stamps/ |archive-date=November 7, 2017}}</ref>

Singleton's 2018 season matched the previous year in tackles with 123. Although he recorded no [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], Singleton did add 6 special teams tackles for the Stamps, as well as 2 forced fumbles and was named to his second CFL All-Star team.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.cfl.ca/2018/11/07/star-power-2018-cfl-divisional-stars-announced/| title = Star Power: 2018 CFL Divisional All-Stars announced - CFL.ca| date = November 7, 2018}}</ref><ref name="2018 allstars">{{Cite web |title=Stars aligned: 2018 CFL All-Stars unveiled |date=December 4, 2018 |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2018/12/04/stars-aligned-2018-cfl-stars-unveiled/ |access-date=December 4, 2018 |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]]}}</ref> On January 7, Singleton was released by the Stampeders so he could pursue NFL opportunities.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://calgarysun.com/sports/football/cfl/calgary-stampeders/singleton-released-by-stamps-to-pursue-nfl-options|title=Singleton released by Stamps to pursue NFL job}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:Alex Singleton (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Singleton with the Eagles in 2021]]

On January 7, 2019, Singleton signed with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] along with CFL teammate [[Marken Michel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Erby |first=Glenn |date=January 8, 2019 |title=Eagles sign star CFL LB Alex Singleton to reserve/futures deal |url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/2019/01/08/eagles-sign-star-cfl-lb-alex-singleton-to-reserve-futures-deal/ |access-date=November 6, 2020 |website=Eagles Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

Singleton played in all four preseason games for the Eagles, and contributed with 28 defensive tackles and one forced fumble. He was waived during final roster cuts on August 30, 2019,<ref>{{cite news |date=August 30, 2019 |title=Eagles announce first wave of roster moves as team works toward 53-player limit |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-roster-cutdown-2019 |access-date=August 30, 2019}}</ref> but was re-signed to the team's practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite news |last=McPherson, Chris |date=September 1, 2019 |title=Eagles agree to terms with nine practice squad players |work=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-terms-with-nine-practice-squad-players |access-date=September 1, 2019}}</ref> On October 16, 2019, Singleton was promoted to the active roster following the release of linebacker [[Zach Brown]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=October 16, 2019 |title=Eagles promote Alex Singleton |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/eagles-promote-alex-singleton-223558037.html |access-date=November 6, 2020 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> He played in 10 games, only on special teams.

In Week 4 of 2020 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'', Singleton went into the game on defense due to an injury to [[T. J. Edwards]]. With less than 6 minutes remaining in the game, Singleton recorded his first career [[interception]] off a pass thrown by [[Nick Mullens]] and returned it for a 30-yard touchdown during the 25–20 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at San Francisco 49ers – October 4th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010040sfo.htm |access-date=October 6, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> By Week 6, Singleton became a starting linebacker for the Eagles. In Week 11 against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Singleton led the team with 12 tackles, sacked [[Baker Mayfield]] once, and recovered a fumble lost by Mayfield during the 22–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Cleveland Browns - November 22nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011220cle.htm |access-date=November 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 17 against the [[Washington Football Team]] on ''Sunday Night Football'', Singleton led the team with 14 tackles and sacked [[Alex Smith]] once during the 20–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Football Team at Philadelphia Eagles - January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030phi.htm |access-date=January 7, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Overall, Singleton played in all regular season games with 11 starts and led the Eagles in tackles at 120. As a result, he earned an additional $464,296 through performance-based pay.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Singleton led Eagles in performance-based pay for 2020 season |date=April 6, 2021 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/alex-singleton-led-eagles-performance-based-pay-2020-season}}</ref>

On March 1, the Eagles placed a one-year [[exclusive-rights free agent]] tender on Singleton, which he signed on March 25, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |author=Erby, Glenn |title=Alex Singleton under contract for 2021 season after signing exclusive rights tender |url=https://theeagleswire.usatoday.com/2021/03/25/alex-singleton-philadelphia-eagles-nfl-free-agency-tender/ |website=USA Today |date=March 25, 2021 |access-date=March 25, 2021}}</ref> On September 6, it was announced that he was voted by his teammates to be a team captain for the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite news|last=McPherson|first=Chris|date=September 6, 2021|title=Eagles name 2021 captains|url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-name-2021-captains}}</ref> After initially playing at the starting linebacker position, he was relegated to backup and replaced by [[Davion Taylor]] in Week 6. He was put back into the starting position in Week 12 after an injury to Taylor.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/what-eagles-lb-alex-singleton-thought-about-when-he-got-benched |title=What Eagles LB Alex Singleton thought about when he got benched|date=November 27, 2021 }}</ref> In Week 16 against the [[New York Giants]], he caught an interception off a deflection from [[Rodney McLeod]] and returned it for a 29-yard touchdown, his second career pick-6.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://3downnation.com/2021/12/26/to-the-house-alex-singleton-records-second-career-nfl-pick-six/|title=To the House! Alex Singleton records second career NFL pick-six|date=December 26, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on the [[COVID-19]] list on January 3, 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Eagles place 12 players on Reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-place-12-players-on-reserve-covid-19-list |author=Oddo, Jillian |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> He was activated one week later on January 10, missing just one game where the Eagles did not play their starters as they had already clinched a playoff spot.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles Clear COVID List, Place Three on IR|url=https://www.sportstalkphilly.com/2022/01/eagles-clear-covid-list-place-three-on-ir.html|author=Bowman, Paul|website=SportsTalkPhilly.com|date=January 10, 2022|access-date=January 10, 2022|archive-date=January 10, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220110220132/https://www.sportstalkphilly.com/2022/01/eagles-clear-covid-list-place-three-on-ir.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Singleton finished the season as the team's leading tackler for the 2nd year in a row with 137, the most in a single season by any Eagle since [[Byron Evans]] in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SingAl00.htm|title=Alex Singleton Pro Football Reference|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> In the wild card game against the Buccaneers, Singleton led the team in tackles with 16, which included 4 tackles for loss and one sack in the 31–15 loss.

===Denver Broncos===
[[File:Singleton 2025.png|thumb|Singleton with the [[Denver Broncos]] in 2025]]
On March 18, 2022, Singleton signed a one-year contract with the [[Denver Broncos]] reportedly worth $1.1 million guaranteed with $750k in playing time incentives.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos agree to terms with LB Singleton on one-year deal |date=March 18, 2022 |url=https://www.tsn.ca/denver-broncos-alex-singleton-one-year-1-1m-deal-1.1773076}}</ref> The move reunited him with quarterback [[Russell Wilson]], whom Singleton had formed a relationship with during his short stint in Seattle.<ref name="y298">{{cite web | last=Heath | first=Jon | title=Broncos LB Alex Singleton happy to reunite with QB Russell Wilson | website=Broncos Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2022-03-25 | url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2022/03/25/denver-broncos-alex-singleton-russell-wilson-reunion/ | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref>

On October 17, 2022, during a Week 6 game against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], Singleton recorded 19 solo tackles and a total of 21 combined tackles in the 19–16 overtime loss. His 19 solo tackles tied [[Derrick Brooks]] for the second-most solo tackles in a single game in NFL history.<ref>{{cite web|title=NFL Tackles single game leaders (since 1994)|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/leaders/tackles_solo_single_game.htm}}</ref> Despite an underwhelming season for the Broncos, Singleton had a career year, ranking 5th in combined tackles during the season with 163.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Defense |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/defense.htm |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 13, 2023, Singleton signed a three-year, $18 million contract extension with $9 million guaranteed.<ref name="s141">{{cite web | title=Denver Broncos re-sign former CFL LB Alex Singleton to $18-million contract | website=3DownNation | date=2023-03-13 | url=https://3downnation.com/2023/03/13/denver-broncos-re-sign-former-cfl-lb-alex-singleton-to-18-million-contract/ | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos re-sign ILB Alex Singleton|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-re-sign-ilb-alex-singleton|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=March 16, 2023}}</ref>

Prior to the [[2024 NFL season|2024 season]], Singleton was voted a [[Captain (American football)|captain]] by his teammates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Adam |date=2024-09-04 |title=Bo Nix Named Broncos Team Captain for 2024 NFL Season Ahead of Rookie Debut |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10134187-bo-nix-named-broncos-team-captain-for-2024-nfl-season-ahead-of-rookie-debut |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=Bleacher Report }}</ref> On the opening drive of the Broncos' Week 1 game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Singleton intercepted a pass by [[Geno Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-08 |title=ILB Alex Singleton snags Broncos' first interception of 2024 {{!}} Broncos at Seahawks |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/video/ilb-alex-singleton-snags-broncos-first-interception-of-2024-broncos-at-seahawks |access-date=2024-09-26 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref> In Week 3 against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Singleton ruptured his [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]]. Singleton still managed to play every defensive snap for the rest of the game despite his injury occurring in the 1st quarter. He was subsequently placed on season-ending injured reserve on September 25.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Podell |first=Garrett |date=2024-09-25 |title=Broncos leading tackler Alex Singleton out for season with ACL tear; LB played majority of Week 3 with injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/broncos-leading-tackler-alex-singleton-out-for-season-with-acl-tear-lb-played-majority-of-week-3-with-injury/ |access-date=2024-09-25 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref>

During the 2025 season, Singleton started 16 games and led the Broncos with 135 Tackles en route to being named as an alternate for the 2025 Pro Bowl.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomasson |first=Chris |date=December 23, 2025 |title=6 Broncos players named to Pro Bowl, including Pat Surtain for 4th straight season |url=https://gazette.com/2025/12/23/6-broncos-players-named-to-pro-bowl-including-pat-surtain-for-4th-straight-season/ |access-date=January 26, 2026 |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |language=en-US}}</ref>  On January 17, 2026, during their divisional playoff game against the [[Buffalo Bills]] and with Denver already trailing while Buffalo was driving to score, Singleton tackled Bills running back [[James Cook (running back)|James Cook]] and forced a fumble which was recovered by teammate [[Talanoa Hufanga]]. The play shifted the momentum of the game in Denver's favor and they ultimately won 33–30 in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=2026-01-22 |title=Singleton after season-best 14 tackles: 'When not battling cancer, you can play football better' |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/nfl/denver-broncos/mike-klis/denver-broncos-alex-singleton/73-c72afcc9-9342-4ede-8879-da979c119c1b |access-date=2026-01-22 |website=9news.com}}</ref>

On March 10, 2026, Singleton signed a two-year. $15.5 million contract extension with the Broncos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos re-sign ILB Alex Singleton to 2-year contract|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-re-sign-ilb-alex-singleton-to-2-year-contract|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=March 10, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Singleton's older sister Ashley was born with [[Down syndrome]]. She participates as a [[Special Olympics]] athlete and has won multiple gold medals. Due to their relationship, Singleton is a major advocate for the Special Olympics and other disability-friendly events.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinney |first=Ellie |date=2022-11-29 |title=Inspired by his sister, ILB Alex Singleton represents Special Olympics for My Cause My Cleats |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/inspired-by-his-sister-ilb-alex-singleton-represents-special-olympics-for-my-cau |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=Denver Broncos }}</ref>

On November 3, 2025, Singleton was diagnosed with [[testicular cancer]] after taking a random drug test a few days previously that showed an elevated [[human chorionic gonadotropin]] level. He underwent surgery for the cancer to be removed on November 7.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-10 |title=LB Singleton has surgery for testicular cancer |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46919305/broncos-lb-alex-singleton-surgery-testicular-cancer |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-11-10 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/american-football/articles/czxk5l5pwkko|title=Nine tackles on Thursday, cancer surgery on Friday for Broncos' Singleton}}</ref> Singleton subsequently received the Broncos' 2025 [[Ed Block Courage Award]] for playing in Week 10 against the Raiders despite his condition.

'''Alex Lewis''' (born April 21, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]], and was selected by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in the fourth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Lewis started his career with [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado]], playing all 12 games as a [[true freshman]] in [[2011 Colorado Buffaloes football team|2011]] at [[tackle (American football position)|tackle]] and [[tight end]] before moving to [[guard (American football)|guard]]. He played all of the [[2012 Colorado Buffaloes football team|2012 season]] at left guard.

After the 2012 season, Lewis transferred to [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], where his father, [[Bill Lewis (center)|Bill Lewis]], was an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] center. He sat out the 2013 season due to transfer rules and started all games for Nebraska in [[2014 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team|2014]] and [[2015 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team|2015]].
