===Baltimore Ravens===
The [[Baltimore Ravens]] selected Lewis with the 130th overall pick in the fourth round of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-draft/Round-4-Ravens-Draft-OT-Alex-Lewis-At-No-130/84277b35-c66f-4126-a2a6-fff5d7fd41f4|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170812060148/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-draft/Round-4-Ravens-Draft-OT-Alex-Lewis-At-No-130/84277b35-c66f-4126-a2a6-fff5d7fd41f4|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 12, 2017|title=Round 4: Ravens Draft OT Alex Lewis At No. 130|work=BaltimoreRavens.com|first=Garrett|last=Downing|date=April 30, 2016}}</ref> He played in 10 games with 8 starts at guard for the Ravens before missing the last six weeks of the season with a sprained ankle.

On August 10, 2017, during the Ravens first preseason games, Lewis suffered a shoulder injury that required surgery, causing him to miss the entire 2017 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Injury Updates On Joe Flacco, Alex Lewis, Tim White|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Injury-Updates-on-Joe-Flacco-Alex-Lewis-Tim-White/2a0e540e-c1a7-4076-9d2f-220e441fa4a6|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119023702/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Injury-Updates-on-Joe-Flacco-Alex-Lewis-Tim-White/2a0e540e-c1a7-4076-9d2f-220e441fa4a6|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2018|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=August 11, 2017}}</ref> He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on September 1, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens Announce 24 Roster Moves, Have 13 More To Make|url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Announce-24-Roster-Moves-Have-13-More-to-Make/914aba64-f454-47d9-932f-e409ccec1735|author=Mink, Ryan|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|date=September 1, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180118220814/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Announce-24-Roster-Moves-Have-14-More-to-Make/914aba64-f454-47d9-932f-e409ccec1735|archive-date=January 18, 2018}}</ref>

On October 14, 2018, Lewis was carted off field with a suspected serious neck injury.<ref>{{cite web | last=Stevens | first=Matthew | title=Ravens G Alex Lewis carted off field, headed to hospital with neck injury | website=Ravens Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=October 14, 2018 | url=https://ravenswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/ravens/2018/10/14/ravens-g-alex-lewis-carted-off-field-with-an-apparent-neck-injury/80647549007/ | access-date=April 14, 2026}}</ref> He only missed two games and returned in Week 9.

===New York Jets===
On August 5, 2019, Lewis was traded to the [[New York Jets]] for a conditional seventh round draft pick in the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Scott |first1=Jelani |title=Ravens pivot, deal Alex Lewis to Jets for 2020 pick |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001039078/article/ravens-pivot-deal-alex-lewis-to-jets-for-2020-pick |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190805204908/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000001039078/article/ravens-pivot-deal-alex-lewis-to-jets-for-2020-pick |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 5, 2019 |website=NFL.com |access-date=August 5, 2019}}</ref> After beginning the season as a backup, he was named the starting left guard in Week 5 following an injury to [[Kelechi Osemele]]. He started 12 games before being placed on injured reserve on December 28, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets claim TE Ross Travis off waivers from Colts, place Alex Lewis on IR|url=https://jetswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/29/jets-ross-travis-colts-claim-waivers-alex-lewis-injured-reserve/|work=Jets Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=December 28, 2019}}</ref>

On March 21, 2020, Lewis signed a three-year, $18.6 million contract extension with the Jets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets re-sign Alex Lewis|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/03/17/jets-re-sign-alex-lewis/|author=Alper, Josh|work=Pro Football Talk|publisher=NBC Sports|date=March 17, 2020}}</ref> He started nine games at left guard before being placed on the reserve/[[non-football injury list]] on December 4, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Place LG Alex Lewis on Non-Football Injury List|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-lg-alex-lewis-on-non-football-injury-list|author=Greenberg, Ethan|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=December 4, 2020}}</ref> He was designated to return and began practicing with the team again on December 30, but the team did not activate him before the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |author=Greenberg, Ethan |title=Jets Designate LG Alex Lewis, RG Greg Van Roten to Return to Practice |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-designate-lg-alex-lewis-rg-greg-van-roten-to-return-to-practice |website=NewYorkJets.com |date=December 30, 2020 |access-date=February 18, 2021}}</ref>

On August 6, 2021, Lewis was placed on the left squad list after injuring his head during practice.<ref>{{cite web |author=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=August 6, 2021 |title=Jets Activate George Fant, Place Alex Lewis on Exempt List |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-george-fant-place-alex-lewis-on-exempt-list |access-date=September 20, 2025 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He announced his retirement on August 18.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=August 18, 2021 |title=Jets guard Alex Lewis retiring |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/jets-guard-alex-lewis-retiring |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Alex McCalister''' (born October 17, 1993) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played college football as a [[defensive end]] at the [[University of Florida]] from 2012 to 2015. He was selected in the seventh round of the [[2016 NFL draft]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].

==College career==
It was reported that McCalister was dismissed from the Florida Gators football team prior to the [[2016 Citrus Bowl (January)|2016 Citrus Bowl]] against [[2015 Michigan Wolverines football team|Michigan]]; however, McCallister in reality never was dismissed and instead was merely injured.<ref>{{cite web|title=WATCH: Eagles' Alex McCalister says Florida didn't kick him off team|url=http://www.nj.com/eagles/index.ssf/2016/05/watch_eagles_alex_mccalister_says_florida_didnt_ki.html|author=Lombardo, Matt|website=NJ.com|date=May 13, 2016}}</ref> He declared for the [[2016 NFL draft]] as an early entrant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ellis |first=Zac |date=January 19, 2016 |title=Picking NFL draft early-entry winners and losers |url=https://www.si.com/college/2016/01/19/nfl-draft-2016-early-entry-decision-winners-losers |access-date=2022-02-24 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
McCalister was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the seventh round, 240th overall, of the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Florida's McCalister Brings Depth To D-Line|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Floridas-McCalister-Brings-Depth-To-D-Line/0846a3df-2a59-4622-9a9a-fc37890a1981|author=Smith, Alex|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=April 30, 2016|access-date=September 8, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909053335/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Floridas-McCalister-Brings-Depth-To-D-Line/0846a3df-2a59-4622-9a9a-fc37890a1981|archive-date=September 9, 2017}}</ref> On August 28, 2016, the Eagles placed McCalister on [[injured reserve]] with a calf strain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles announce 10 roster moves, including some surprising cuts|url=http://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2016/8/28/12684172/eagles-rueben-randle-roster-nfl-cuts-moves-philadelphia-depth-chart|author=Gowton, Brandon Lee|website=BleedingGreenNation.com|date=August 28, 2016}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, McCalister was waived by the Eagles.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles Announce 17 Roster Moves To Get Down To 53 Players|url=http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Announce-17-Roster-Moves-To-Get-Down-To-53-Players/e9f17d13-6a84-4b71-a56e-3806e03a2aa0|website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905051907/http://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/article-1/Eagles-Announce-17-Roster-Moves-To-Get-Down-To-53-Players/e9f17d13-6a84-4b71-a56e-3806e03a2aa0|archive-date=September 5, 2017}}</ref> He was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] on October 10, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia Eagles bring back 2016 draft pick to practice squad|url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2017/10/10/16455548/alex-mccalister-philadelphia-eagles-sign-2016-draft-pick-practice-squad-defensive-end-florida-gators|author=Gowton, Brandon Lee|website=BleedingGreenNation.com|date=October 10, 2017}}</ref> He was released by the team on October 24, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Eagles cut DE Alex McCalister from practice squad|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/philadelphia-eagles/article/eagles-cut-de-alex-mccalister-from-practice-squad-109422008/|website=247Sports.com|date=October 25, 2017}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
McCalister was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad on December 12, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|website=Redskins.com|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Place-Three-On-Injured-Reserve-Sign-Three-To-Active-Roster/530f7415-c0f8-43e6-a98c-071a84d015ca|title=Redskins Place Three On Injured Reserve, Sign Three To Active Roster|first=Stephen|last=Czarda|date=December 12, 2017|access-date=December 12, 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104202627/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Place-Three-On-Injured-Reserve-Sign-Three-To-Active-Roster/530f7415-c0f8-43e6-a98c-071a84d015ca|archive-date=January 4, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Redskins on January 1, 2018, but was waived on August 6.<ref>{{cite web|title=Redskins Sign 11 Players To Reserve/Future Contracts|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-11-Players-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/c6f20f93-73d6-4275-9173-5e8d96ee85b0|website=Redskins.com|date=January 1, 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103202113/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-11-Players-To-ReserveFuture-Contracts/c6f20f93-73d6-4275-9173-5e8d96ee85b0|archive-date=January 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=8/6: Redskins Make Roster Moves |url=https://www.redskins.com/news/8-6-redskins-make-roster-moves |website=Redskins.com |date=August 6, 2018 |access-date=August 6, 2018 |archive-date=August 6, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806200258/https://www.redskins.com/news/8-6-redskins-make-roster-moves |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (first stint)===
McCalister signed with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on February 15, 2019, but was released during final roster cuts on June 9.

===Columbus Destroyers===
McCalister was assigned to the [[Columbus Destroyers]] of the [[Arena Football League]] on July 9, 2019.<ref name="Col">{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/teams/?page=transactions&type=old&team=240#google_vignette | title=Historical Team Transactions | publisher=ArenaFan.com | accessdate=30 April 2025}}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers (second stint)===
McCalister was signed to the Blue Bombers' active roster on August 20. He was released on June 1, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |title=2021 CFL Transactions |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/?season=2021 |website=CFL.ca |access-date=June 4, 2021}}</ref>

===BC Lions===
On December 15, 2022, McCalister signed with the [[BC Lions]] of the CFL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/ |title=Transactions – Football player trades and signings |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=May 21, 2023}}</ref> On May 31, 2023, McCalister was released by the Lions.

'''Alex Michael Erickson''' (born November 6, 1992) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] and [[return specialist]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin Badgers]] and was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2016. Erickson has also been a member of the [[Houston Texans]], [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Washington Commanders]], [[New York Jets]], [[Los Angeles Chargers]] and [[New England Patriots]].

==Early life==
At Darlington High School, Erickson rushed for 3,856 yards and 57 [[touchdowns]], passed for 3,648 yards and 37 touchdowns and recorded 170 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]] and 14 ===Cincinnati Bengals===
Erickson signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] as an undrafted free agent in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 16, 2016 |title=Former Badgers receiver Erickson fitting in with Bengals |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/former-badgers-receiver-erickson-fitting-in-with-bengals |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US |archive-date=January 19, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119032802/https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/former-badgers-receiver-erickson-fitting-in-with-bengals |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Harvey, Coley |date=August 13, 2016 |title=As Bengals' WR race heats up, get to know the elusive Alex Erickson |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/23340/alex-erickson-bengals-mario-alford-wr-race-heats-up-get-to-know-elusive/ |access-date=April 19, 2017 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=February 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190210070322/http://www.espn.com/blog/cincinnati-bengals/post/_/id/23340/alex-erickson-bengals-mario-alford-wr-race-heats-up-get-to-know-elusive |url-status=live }}</ref> He was the only undrafted free agent to make the Bengals' final roster.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Erickson |url=https://www.bengals.com/team/players-roster/alex-erickson/career?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=www.bengals.com |language=en-US }}{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

He started the season as the team's primary kick returner and punt returner, a spot he continued throughout the season, and as a backup receiver.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2016 |title=Alex Erickson, the coolest story in Cincy |url=http://www.buckys5thquarter.com/2016/8/30/12714106/alex-erickson-the-coolest-story-in-cincy |access-date=April 19, 2017 |website=Buckys5thQuarter.com |archive-date=August 9, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809210521/https://www.buckys5thquarter.com/2016/8/30/12714106/alex-erickson-the-coolest-story-in-cincy |url-status=live }}</ref> For the season, he had 6 catches for 71 yards, and averaged 27.9 yards per [[kickoff return]] and 7.0 yards per punt return.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Erickson 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093758/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live }}</ref>  His 810 kickoff return yards led the NFL in that category.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Kick & Punt Returns |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/returns.htm |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 28, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180428093800/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2016/returns.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On November 19, 2017, Erickson recorded his first NFL touchdown, scoring on a 29-yard pass from [[Andy Dalton]] during the Bengals 20–17 victory over the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Denver Broncos - November 19th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711190den.htm |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818091809/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711190den.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2017 season with 12 receptions for 180 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown to go along with 32 kick returns for 663 net yards and 39 punt returns for 278 net yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Erickson 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 27, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110014227/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 8, 2018, Erickson signed a two-year contract extension with the Bengals through the 2020 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=September 8, 2018 |title=Bengals sign returner Alex Erickson to extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-sign-returner-alex-erickson-to-extension-0ap3000000959171 |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=March 26, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190326072949/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000959171/article/bengals-sign-returner-alex-erickson-to-extension |url-status=live }}</ref> He finished the 2018 season with 20 receptions for 187 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Erickson 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=March 15, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104181058/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Erickson posted his first career 100+ receiving yard game on October 20, 2019, against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], where he finished with 137 receiving yards as the Bengals lost 17–27.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2019 |title=Minshew, defense lead Jaguars over winless Bengals 27-17 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127945 |access-date=October 20, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=May 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505073604/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127945 |url-status=live }}</ref> Overall, Erickson finished the 2019 season with 43 receptions for 529 receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Erickson 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=April 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=November 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104181105/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EricAl01/gamelog/2019/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
Erickson signed with the [[Washington Commanders]] on May 4, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 4, 2022 |title=Commanders sign WR Alex Erickson |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-wr-alex-erickson |access-date=May 4, 2022 |website=Commanders.com |archive-date=May 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220504164352/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-wr-alex-erickson |url-status=live }}</ref> He was waived on August 30, 2022, and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Commanders cut 25 players, place 3 on IR |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-final-roster-cuts |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Commanders.com |archive-date=September 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901115031/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-final-roster-cuts |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2022 |title=Commanders announce practice squad |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-announce-practice-squad |access-date=November 25, 2022 |website=Commanders.com |archive-date=October 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221006080927/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-announce-practice-squad |url-status=live }}</ref>
He signed a reserve/future contract on January 9, 2023,<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Commanders sign 9 players to Reserve/Future contracts |url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230109220610/https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |archive-date=January 9, 2023 |access-date=January 9, 2023 |website=Commanders.com}}</ref> and was released on May 12, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manning |first=Bryan |date=May 12, 2023 |title=Commanders release 2 players Friday |url=https://commanderswire.usatoday.com/2023/05/12/washington-commanders-rookie-minicamp-release-2-players-friday/ |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=Commanders Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref>

'''Alexander Colby Ellis''' (born February 10, 1993) is an American [[American football|football]] [[tight end]]. He was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an undrafted free agent after the [[2016 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] at [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]].

==College career==
Ellis attended the [[University of Tennessee]], where he played as a [[tight end]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]] football team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Ellis College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-ellis-1.html |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2014 and 2015  seasons, he totaled 14 receptions for 232 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Ellis College Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-ellis-1/gamelog/9999 |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On May 9, 2016, Ellis signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an [[Free agent|undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 9, 2016 |title=Titans Agree to Terms with 11 Undrafted Free Agents |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-agree-to-terms-with-11-undrafted-free-agents-17130755 |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> On September 2, Ellis was waived by the Titans as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Down to 53 Players: A Position-by-Position Look|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TitansOnline.com|date=September 2, 2016|accessdate=May 26, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807023144/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Down-to-53-Players-A-Position-by-Position-Look/628127bc-7013-4906-a04d-bd1f9e8ce8fa|archivedate=August 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On September 5, 2016, Ellis was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]' [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars finalize 10-man practice squad|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-finalize-10-man-practice-squad/1ce26a1a-69fe-4043-b843-208abe962df9|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902180947/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-finalize-10-man-practice-squad/1ce26a1a-69fe-4043-b843-208abe962df9|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 2, 2017|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 5, 2016|accessdate=May 26, 2017}}</ref> On November 26, he was promoted to their active roster, where he played his first NFL game against the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Comeaux |first=Jonathan |date=November 26, 2016 |title=Jaguars Promote TE Alex Ellis To Active Roster & Waive DT Richard Ash |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/jaguars-promote-te-alex-ellis-active-roster-waive-dt-richard-ash/ |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=NFLTradeRumors.co |language=en-US}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Ellis was waived by the Jaguars.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jaguars reduce active roster to 53 players|url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-reduce-active-roster-to-53-players/11928d4a-71bb-4c27-af08-70f67c3242e8|author=Oehser, John|website=Jaguars.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905032258/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/Jaguars-reduce-active-roster-to-53-players/11928d4a-71bb-4c27-af08-70f67c3242e8|archivedate=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
On November 29, 2017, Ellis was signed to the [[New Orleans Saints]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints sign tight end Alex Ellis to practice squad|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2017/11/saints_alex_ellis.html|author=Katzenstein, Josh|website=NOLA.com|date=November 29, 2017}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Saints on January 16, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints sign 10 players, including De'Vante Harris, to reserve/future contracts|url=http://www.nola.com/saints/index.ssf/2018/01/saints_sign_10_players_includi.html|author=Teope, Herbie|website=NOLA.com|date=January 16, 2018}}</ref> On May 7, Ellis was waived by the Saints.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints sign four undrafted rookies, waive four to make room|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/05/07/saints-sign-four-undrafted-rookies-waive-four-others-to-make-room/|author=Williams, Charean|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=May 7, 2018}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On May 8, 2018, Ellis was claimed off waivers by the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Chiefs' Alex Ellis: Claimed by Kansas City|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chiefs-alex-ellis-claimed-by-kansas-city/|website=CBSSports.com|date=May 8, 2018}}</ref> He was waived with an injury designation by the Chiefs on October 2. After going unclaimed on waivers, the Chiefs placed him on [[Injured reserve list|injured reserve]].<ref name="t838">{{cite web | last=Sweeney | first=Pete | title=Chiefs waive TE Alex Ellis, sign free-agent DB Josh Shaw | website=Arrowhead Pride | date=2018-10-02 | url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2018/10/2/17929826/chiefs-waive-te-alex-ellis-sign-free-agent-db-josh-shaw | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Eagles===
On August 2, 2019, Ellis was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McPherson |first=Chris |date=August 2, 2019 |title=Eagles sign TE Alex Ellis |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-te-alex-ellis |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on August 31,<ref>{{cite news |title=Eagles announce roster moves as team gets to 53-player limit |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-roster-cutdown-2019 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=August 31, 2019 |accessdate=August 31, 2019}}</ref> and re-signed to the team's practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite news |author=McPherson, Chris |title=Eagles agree to terms with nine practice squad players |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-agree-to-terms-with-nine-practice-squad-players |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=September 1, 2019 |accessdate=September 1, 2019}}</ref> On September 6, he was promoted to the 53-man roster as the team's third tight end.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McPherson |first1=Chris |title=TE Alex Ellis promoted to active roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/te-alex-ellis-promoted-to-active-roster |website=philadelphiaeagles.com |date=September 6, 2019 |accessdate=September 6, 2019}}</ref> He was waived again on September 10,<ref>{{cite news |author=Spadaro, Dave |title=Eagles agree to terms with DT Akeem Spence as defensive line prepares to move on without Malik Jackson |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/defensive-line-prepares-to-move-on-without-malik-jackson |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=September 10, 2019 |accessdate=September 10, 2019}}</ref> and re-signed to the team's practice squad on September 11. He was promoted to the team's active roster again on September 17.<ref>{{cite news |author=Alper, Josh |title=Eagles promote Alex Ellis, waive Craig James |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/09/17/eagles-promote-alex-ellis-waive-craig-james/ |website=NBCSports.com |date=September 17, 2019 |accessdate=September 17, 2019}}</ref> After suffering a knee injury in Week 4 against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Ellis was waived/injured on October 4,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schaller |first=Olivia |date=October 4, 2019 |title=Eagles promote CB Ryan Lewis from the practice squad |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-promote-cb-ryan-lewis-from-the-practice-squad |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> and subsequently reverted to the team's injured reserve list after clearing waivers on October 7. He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on October 15. He was re-signed to the practice squad on December 16. He signed a reserve/future contract with the Eagles on January 6, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schaller |first=Olivia |date=January 6, 2020 |title=Eagles sign eight practice squad players to futures deals |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-sign-eight-practice-squad-players-to-futures-deals |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Ellis was waived by the Eagles on July 17.<ref>{{cite news |author=McPherson, Chris |title=Eagles officially sign guard Jason Peters; waive tight end Alex Ellis |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-officially-sign-guard-jason-peters-waive-tight-end-alex-ellis |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com |date=July 17, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

'''Alejandro Barrett''' (born March 6, 1994) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs football|San Diego State Aztecs]].

==Early life==
Barrett was born on March 6, 1994, in [[Yuma, Arizona]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://kyma.com/news/top-stories/2024/02/10/yuma-born-alex-barrett-looks-to-make-local-history/|title=Self-belief, persistence paying off for 49ers Barrett|publisher=[[KYMA]]|first1=Scott|last1=Gross|first2=Chas|last2=Messman|first3=Luis|last3=Lopez|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=April 15, 2025}}</ref> He played [[high school football]] at [[Desert Ridge High School]] in [[Mesa, Arizona]], and earned first-team all-state honors twice. He also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] in track and field at Desert Ridge.<ref name="azt">{{cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/AlexBarrettFinalBio.pdf |title=Alex Barrett |publisher=grfx.cstv.com |access-date=October 8, 2017 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009002143/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-footbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/AlexBarrettFinalBio.pdf |archive-date=October 9, 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Barrett played for the [[San Diego State Aztecs football|San Diego State Aztecs]] of [[San Diego State University]] from 2013 to 2016. He was [[redshirted]] in 2012. He played in 12 games in 2013, recording 8 solo tackles, 7 tackle assists and 3 sacks. He played in 10 games, all starts, in 2014, recording 21 solo tackles, 18 tackle assists, 3 sacks, 3 pass breakups and 1 forced fumble. Barrett earned Honorable Mention All-[[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] honors in 2014. He played in 14 games, all starts, in 2015, totaling 33 solo tackles, 29 tackle assists, 5.5 sacks, 2 interceptions, 1 pass breakup and 2 forced fumbles. He was named First-team All-Mountain West in 2015. Barrett played in 14 games, all starts, in 2016, recording 29 solo tackles, 24 tackle assists, 7.5 sacks and 4 pass breakups. He garnered First-team All-Mountain West recognition in 2016, becoming the first San Diego State defensive lineman to earn First-team All-Mountain West honors multiple times. He was also a team captain his senior year in 2016. Barrett played in 50 games, starting 38, during his college career, totaling 91 solo tackles, 78 tackle assists, 19 sacks, 2 interceptions, 8 pass breakups, and 3 forced fumbles. His 19 sacks were tied for the fourth most in school history.<ref name="azt"/>

'''Alex Edward Redmond''' (born January 18, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]].

==Early life==
Redmond played [[high school football]] at [[Los Alamitos High School]] in [[Los Alamitos, California]]. He also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] three years in wrestling at Los Alamitos, becoming the first wrestling state finalist in school history.<ref name="ucla">{{cite web | url=http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3870 | title=Alex Redmond | publisher=uclabruins.com | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017023428/http://www.uclabruins.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3870 | access-date=October 9, 2017| archive-date=October 17, 2017 }}</ref>

==College career==
Redmond played for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], from 2013 to 2015. He started all 13 games at right guard in 2013, tying the school record for most single-season starts by a true freshman position player. He earned Honorable Mention [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12]] honors in 2013. Redmond was also named a First Team Freshman [[All-American]] by the [[Sporting News]], [[Athlon Sports]] and the [[Football Writers Association of America]]. He started eight games at right guard in 2014, earning Honorable Mention All-Pac-12 honors. He played in 12 games, starting 10, in 2015.<ref name="ucla"/> Redmond was declared academically ineligible prior to the team's final game of the 2015 season, the [[2015 Foster Farms Bowl|Foster Farms Bowl]].<ref name="Hammond">{{cite web | url=http://www.ocregister.com/2016/02/25/ex-ucla-los-alamitos-lineman-alex-redmond-explains-departure-from-bruins/ | title=Ex-UCLA, Los Alamitos lineman Alex Redmond explains departure from Bruins | publisher=ocregister.com | date=February 25, 2016 | access-date=October 10, 2017 | author=Hammond, Rich| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010191051/http://www.ocregister.com/2016/02/25/ex-ucla-los-alamitos-lineman-alex-redmond-explains-departure-from-bruins/ | archive-date=October 10, 2017 }}</ref> He also declared for the [[2016 NFL draft]] prior to the game.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/college-football/2015/12/23/ucla-bruins-alex-redmond-nfl-draft | title=UCLA OL Alex Redmond declares for draft, to skip Foster Farms Bowl | publisher=si.com | date=December 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010185458/https://www.si.com/college-football/2015/12/23/ucla-bruins-alex-redmond-nfl-draft | access-date=October 10, 2017| archive-date=October 10, 2017 }}</ref> However, Redmond stated that he had always planned to enter the draft after three years. He also said that turning professional would help him support his daughter.<ref name="Hammond"/> He majored in history at UCLA.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/uclabruins.com/documents/2015/8/13/FB_15MG_FULL.pdf | title=2015 UCLA FOOTBALL | publisher=amazonaws.com | access-date=October 10, 2017 | pages=37| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010192007/https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/uclabruins.com/documents/2015/8/13/FB_15MG_FULL.pdf | archive-date=October 10, 2017 }}</ref>

==Professional career==
Redmond was rated the 21st best offensive guard in the 2016 NFL Draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref name="draft"/> [[Lance Zierlein]] of NFL.com predicted that he would be drafted in the seventh round or be a priority free agent.<ref name="nfldraft">{{cite web | url=http://www.nfl.com/draft/2016/profiles/alex-redmond?id=2555493 | title=Alex Redmond | work=[[NFL.com]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010182455/http://www.nfl.com/draft/2016/profiles/alex-redmond?id=2555493 | access-date=October 10, 2017| archive-date=October 10, 2017 }}</ref>

On May 17, 2021, Redmond signed with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Sign Offensive Lineman James Ferentz and Alex Redmond|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-offensive-lineman-james-ferentz-and-alex-redmond|website=Patriots.com|date=May 17, 2021}}</ref> He was released on August 31, 2021 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Make Roster Moves to Reach 53-Man Roster Limit; Acquire OL Yasir Durant in a Trade with Kansas City|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves-to-reach-53-man-roster-limit-acquire-ol-yasir-durant-|website=Patriots.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patriots Sign 12 Players to the Practice Squad|url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-sign-12-players-to-the-practice-squad|website=Patriots.com|date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

'''Alex Cappa''' (born January 27, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Humboldt State Lumberjacks football|Humboldt State Lumberjacks]] and was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the third round of the [[2018 NFL draft]].

==College career==
During Cappa's time at [[Humboldt State University]] (now Cal Poly Humboldt), he was named the [[Great Northwest Athletic Conference]] (GNAC) [[offensive lineman]] of the year for 4 years in a row.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Penza |first=Danny |date=November 16, 2016 |title=HSU's Alex Cappa named GNAC Offensive Lineman of the Year for third straight season |url=http://www.times-standard.com/article/NJ/20161115/SPORTS/161119880 |access-date=April 3, 2018 |work=Eureka Times-Standard}}</ref> He was also named to the First-team GNAC every year of his playing career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Penza |first=Danny |date=November 15, 2017 |title=Alex Cappa, Ja'Quan Gardner headline Humboldt State football's all-conference award haul |url=http://www.times-standard.com/article/NJ/20171115/SPORTS/171119899 |access-date=April 3, 2018 |work=Eureka Times-Standard}}</ref> Following his senior season, Cappa was invited to the [[2018 Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Penza, Danny |date=November 28, 2017 |title=Humboldt State left tackle Alex Cappa eager to show his talent after getting Senior Bowl invite |url=http://www.times-standard.com/article/NJ/20171128/sports/171129848 |access-date=April 3, 2018 |work=Eureka Times-Standard}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===

==== 2018 ====
The [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] selected Cappa in the third round with the 94th overall pick in the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> The Buccaneers traded their fourth (102nd overall) and sixth round picks (180th overall) in the 2018 NFL Draft to the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in exchange for the Vikings' third round pick to draft Cappa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Auman |first=Greg |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Bucs trade back into 3rd round, grab Humboldt State OL Alex Cappa |url=https://www.tampabay.com/blogs/bucs/2018/04/27/bucs-trade-back-into-3rd-round-grab-humboldt-state-ol-alex-cappa/ |access-date=August 19, 2018 |website=TampaBay.com}}</ref> Cappa was the 12th offensive tackle drafted in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2018/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-17 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He became Humboldt State's highest draft selection in school history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thorman |first=Joel |date=April 27, 2018 |title=Bucs draft OT Alex Cappa out of Humboldt State |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2018/4/27/17294544/bucs-draft-ot-alex-cappa-out-of-humboldt-state |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=Bucs Nation}}</ref> He also holds the distinction of being Humboldt State's 11th player drafted and the first player selected in the [[NFL draft]] since Freeman Baysinger in [[1992 NFL draft|1992]], as well as being the final player drafted from Humboldt State as the school discontinued its football program after 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Football Database: Humboldt State |url=https://www.footballdb.com/draft/college.html?c=Humboldt+State |access-date=August 19, 2018 |website=footballdb.com}}</ref>

{{external media
| video1 =
[http://www.nfl.com/videos/nfl-draft/0ap3000000929680/Buccaneers-select-Alex-Cappa-No-94-in-the-2018-NFL-Draft Buccaneers draft Alex Cappa 94th overall]
}}
On May 13, 2018, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed Cappa to a four-year, [[United States dollar|$]]3.36 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $793,704.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Alex Cappa contract |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/tampa-bay-buccaneers/alex-cappa-25193/ |access-date=August 18, 2018 |website=spotrac.com}}</ref> As a rookie, Cappa appeared in six games, all at the end of the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Cappa 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CappAl00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

==== 2019 ====
Cappa made his first career start in the 2019 regular season opener against the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers – September 8th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201909080tam.htm |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In a game against the [[New Orleans Saints]] on October 6, 2019, Cappa suffered a broken left arm but did not miss a snap after sustaining the injury in the second quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |title=Buccaneers OL Alex Cappa breaks arm vs. Saints, plays through rest of game |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/buccaneers/2019/10/07/nfl-tampa-bay-buccaneers-alex-cappa-broken-arm-saints/3899292002/ |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=USA TODAY}}</ref>

==== 2020 ====
During the COVID-19 outbreak Cappa was involved with supporting local restaurants and businesses.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stroud |first=Rick |title=One Buc's support of Tampa Bay restaurants sparks circle of giving |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2020/04/15/one-bucs-support-of-local-restaurants-sparks-circle-of-giving/ |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=Tampa Bay Times}}</ref>

On January 9, 2021, in the Wild Card Round against the [[Washington Football Team]], Cappa suffered a fractured ankle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 10, 2021 |title=Bucs fear fractured ankle for G Alex Cappa |url=https://bucswire.usatoday.com/2021/01/10/alex-cappa-injury-update-nfl-playoffs-wild-card-nfc-bucs-washington/ |access-date=March 12, 2021 |work=Bucs Wire}}</ref> On January 15, 2021, Cappa was placed on injured reserve due to the injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=January 15, 2021 |title=Bucs Place Alex Cappa on IR, Bring Earl Watford Back |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-place-alex-cappa-injured-reserve-sign-earl-watford-roster-move |access-date=March 12, 2021 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> The Buccaneers went on to win [[Super Bowl LV]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=February 7, 2017 |title=What we learned from Buccaneers win over Chiefs in Super Bowl LV |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/what-we-learned-from-buccaneers-win-over-chiefs-in-super-bowl-lv |access-date=March 11, 2021 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LV – Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Kansas City Chiefs – February 7th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202102070tam.htm |access-date=March 11, 2021 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2021====
Cappa started all 19 games, regular season and playoffs, and was the only player to be on the field for all 1328 offensive snaps. He had his best season in 2021, helping the Buccaneers allow only 23 sacks and a 3.15% sacks per pass play rate, with both stats leading the league. In addition, the Buccaneers averaged 4.89 yards per carry while running over right guard.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-2022-guard-alex-cappa-free-agent-focus |title=2022 Buccaneers Free Agent Focus: Alex Cappa |date=February 17, 2022 |last=Smith |first=Scott |website=buccaneers.com}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
====2022====
Cappa signed a four-year, $35 million contract with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on March 18, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|work=Bengals.com|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-roster-moves-x4967|title=Bengals Roster Moves|date=March 18, 2022|accessdate=March 20, 2022}}</ref> Cappa was the starting right guard in all 17 regular season games for Cincinnati in 2022, helping the team to a 12–4 record,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Vrentas |first=Jenny |date=2023-01-06 |title=N.F.L. Cancels Bills-Bengals Game |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/05/sports/football/bills-bengals-game-canceled.html |access-date=2023-01-06 |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=January 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230106132155/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/01/05/sports/football/bills-bengals-game-canceled.html |url-status=live}}</ref> but he incurred an ankle injury during the finale against the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. Cappa did not return for the postseason run, in which the Bengals lost the AFC Championship game to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Cappa 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CappAl00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Cincinnati Bengals Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/cin/2022.htm |access-date=2024-12-26 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2023====
Cappa returned as the starting right guard for the 2023 season. He started all 17 games in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Cappa 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CappAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |work=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2024====
Cappa struggled as the starting guard through all 17 games in 2024, finishing last among NFL guards in pressures (51), hurries (36), and sacks allowed (8, tied with [[Shaq Mason]]).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Look: Alex Cappa Takes Home Negative Pass Protection Triple Crown Following 2024 Season|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/bengals/allbengals-insiders-plus/look-alex-cappa-takes-home-negative-pass-protection-triple-crown-following-2024-season-01jh0w9c8enz|access-date=January 15, 2025|website=si.com}}</ref>

On March 3, 2025, Cappa was released by the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bengals Release G Alex Cappa |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-release-g-alex-cappa-bengals-roster-update |website=bengals.com |access-date=4 March 2025}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On March 5, 2025, Cappa signed a two-year, $11 million contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Raiders sign G Alex Cappa|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-alex-cappa-guard-nfl-2025-free-agency-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=March 5, 2025|access-date=March 5, 2025}}</ref>

On March 6, 2026, the Raiders released Cappa.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders release G Alex Cappa|url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-release-ol-alex-cappa-2026-nfl-transactions|website=Raiders.com|date=March 6, 2026}}</ref>

'''Alexander Lee McGough''' ({{IPAc-en|m|ə|ˈ|g|uː}} {{respell|mə|GOO}}; born November 19, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). McGough played [[college football]] for the [[FIU Panthers football|FIU Panthers]],<ref name="Villa">{{Cite news |last=Villa |first=Walter |date=August 7, 2017 |title=Brothers McGough in the middle of things at FIU |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article165884412.html}}</ref> and was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the seventh round of the [[2018 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Green Bay Packers]], and [[Birmingham Stallions]].

==College career==
===2014 season===
On August 30, 2014, McGough made his FIU debut, recording 117 yards and a [[touchdown]] against [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats football|Bethune–Cookman]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kurtenbach |first=Dieter |date=August 30, 2014 |title=FIU loses to Bethune Cookman – again |work=Underdog Dynasty |url=https://www.underdogdynasty.com/2014/8/30/6088849/fiu-loses-to-fcs-bethune-cookman-for-second-straight-year}}</ref> On September 27, he threw an 85-yard and a 75-yard touchdown against [[UAB Blazers football|UAB]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=September 27, 2014 |title=FIU Buckles Down and Beats UAB, 34–20 |work=Underdog Dynasty |url=https://www.underdogdynasty.com/2014/9/27/6855233/fiu-golden-panthers-vs-uab-blazers-recap-2014}}</ref> On November 15, he recorded a season-high 231 yards and three touchdowns against [[Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders football|Middle Tennessee]]. He finished his rookie season recording 1,680 yards and 14 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex McGough 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alex-mcgough-1/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2015 season===
On October 17, 2015, McGough attempted a career-high 51 passes against Middle Tennessee, second most in school history.<ref>{{Cite magazine |date=October 17, 2015 |title=Middle Tennessee holds on to beat Florida Int. 42–34 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |url=https://www.si.com/college-football/2015/10/17/ap-fbc-fiu-middle-tennessee}}</ref> On October 24, McGough recorded a career-best 390 yards (2nd in school history) versus [[Old Dominion Monarchs football|Old Dominion]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 24, 2015 |title=Florida International beats Old Dominion 41–12 |agency=Associated Press |url=https://collegefootball.ap.org/article/florida-international-beats-old-dominion-41-12}}</ref> He completed 31 of 39 passes, good for 2nd most completions and 4th highest percentage in school history.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=FIU Football 2002–2016 |url=https://www.fiusports.com/custompages/Stats/FB/History/histstat.htm?path=football |website=FIUSports.com}}</ref> On November 7, McGough recorded 284 yards and three touchdowns in a 48–31 blowout against [[Charlotte 49ers football|Charlotte]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harper |first=Brian |date=November 7, 2015 |title=FIU gets past Charlotte to keep bowl hopes alive, 48–31 |work=Underdog Dynasty |url=https://www.underdogdynasty.com/2015/11/7/9688742/fiu-gets-past-charlotte-to-keep-bowl-hopes-alive-48-31}}</ref> He finished his second season completing 269 of 420 passes for 2,722 yards and 21 touchdowns, all school records (he broke his record for passing yards in 2017).<ref name=":1" />

===2016 season===
On October 2, 2016, McGough ran for a career-high two touchdowns against [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Villa |first=Walter |date=October 1, 2016 |title=FIU vs. FAU is a rivalry that does not involve shaking hands |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article105485556.html}}</ref> The next week, he threw a season-high 3 touchdowns against [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sparks |first=Bob |date=October 8, 2016 |title=FIU picks up second straight win, beats UTEP 35–21 |work=SaintPetersBlog.com |url=http://saintpetersblog.com/fiu-picks-second-straight-win-beats-utep-35-21/}}</ref> On October 15, McGough threw for a season-high 315 yards and scored three touchdowns, including the game-winner against Charlotte.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kiser |first=Bill |date=October 15, 2016 |title=Alex McGough TD pass to Jonnu Smith with 1:05 left lifts FIU over Charlotte |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article108579792.html}}</ref> He missed the final three games of the season due to a wrist injury.

===2017 season===
On August 31, 2017, McGough threw a 75-yard touchdown pass in the season opener against [[UCF Knights football|UCF]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2017 |title=UCF routs FIU 61–17, spoiling Butch Davis' return |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400938591 |publisher=ESPN |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> The next week, he threw for a season-high 328 yards and runs in a game-winning touchdown against [[Alcorn State Braves football|Alcorn State]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Navarro |first=Manny |date=September 8, 2017 |title=How FIU made Birmingham its new home and got Butch Davis his first win |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article172171722.html}}</ref> On September 30, McGough led the Panthers to a 19-point comeback win over Charlotte, outscoring the 49ers 16–3 in the second half to a 30–29 win.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Butler |first=Alex |date=October 1, 2017 |title=FIU completes 19-point comeback against Charlotte |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article176411676.html}}</ref> On December 2, he threw a season-high three touchdowns and ran for a career-high 108 yards against [[UMass Minutemen football|UMass]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Villa |first=Walter |date=December 2, 2017 |title=In convincing win, FIU football ties, sets school records. This is what's next. |work=Miami Herald |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/conference-usa/florida-international-university/article187767673.html}}</ref> He became the third quarterback in FIU history to run over 100 yards in a game.<ref name=":0" /> He ended his senior season with a completion percentage of 65.3% and a passer rating of 142.8, both school records (previous records were 64% in 2015 by himself & 141.5 rating by Jamie Burke in 2002).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pelegrin |first=Pete |date=December 13, 2017 |title=BEST BYE: Alex McGough has quietly played his best football in his final record-breaking season |url=https://www.fiusports.com/news/2017/12/13/best-bye-alex-mcgough-has-played-his-best-football-in-his-final-season.aspx |website=FIUSports.com}}</ref>

The Panthers finished with an 8–4 record, qualifying for a bowl game for the first time since 2011.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cochrane |first=Karen |date=December 3, 2017 |title=FIU to play Temple Owls in Gasparilla Bowl Dec. 21 |work=FIU News |url=https://news.fiu.edu/2017/12/fiu-to-play-temple-owls-in-gasparilla-bowl-dec-21/117710}}</ref> On December 22, 2017, McGough left in the first quarter of the [[2017 Gasparilla Bowl]] against [[Temple Owls football|Temple]] with a fractured collarbone. The Panthers would go on to lose 28–3.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goodall |first=Fred |date=December 22, 2017 |title=Nutile leads Temple over FIU 28–3 in Gasparilla Bowl |work=AP News |url=https://www.apnews.com/cf1667f95a9142a99cbd2088fa253d36/Nutile-leads-Temple-over-FIU-28-3-in-Gasparilla-Bowl}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
McGough was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the seventh round, 220th overall, of the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=April 28, 2018 |title=Seahawks Draft Florida International Quarterback Alex McGough In Seventh Round Of 2018 NFL Draft |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-draft-florida-international-quarterback-alex-mcgough-in-seventh-round-o |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He was the first quarterback drafted by the Seahawks since [[Russell Wilson]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Matthews |first=Liz Mathews |date=April 29, 2018 |title=Alex McGough is first quarterback drafted by Seahawks since Russell Wilson |work=Seahawks Wire |url=https://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2018/04/29/alex-mcgough-is-seahawks-1st-quarterback-drafted-since-russell-wilson/}}</ref> On May 15, 2018, he signed his rookie contract.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Condotta |first=Bob |date=May 15, 2018 |title=Seahawks sign draft picks Jamarco Jones and Alex McGough |work=The Seattle Times |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-sign-draft-picks-jamarco-jones-and-alex-mcgough/}}</ref> McGough was waived by Seattle on September 1, and was re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Seahawks Set 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-set-53-man-roster |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle, John |date=September 3, 2018 |title=Seahawks Sign 10 To Practice Squad |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-10-to-practice-squad |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
On January 15, 2019, McGough signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Day |first=Ryan |date=January 15, 2019 |title=Jaguars sign Alex McGough to reserve/future contract |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2019/1/15/18184078/jaguars-sign-alex-mcgough-to-reserve-future-contract |access-date=December 19, 2023 |website=Big Cat Country |language=en}}</ref> He was waived by Jacksonville on August 31.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser, John |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Roster reduction: Jaguars move to 53 players |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-reduce-roster-to-53-players |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On September 1, 2019, McGough was signed to the [[Houston Texans]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 2, 2019 |title=Texans sign CB Armstrong, TE Paulsen, add 10 players to practice squad |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-cb-armstrong-te-paulsen-add-10-players-to-practice-squad |website=HoustonTexans.com |access-date=September 3, 2019 |archive-date=September 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903055615/https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-cb-armstrong-te-paulsen-add-10-players-to-practice-squad |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 10.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Texans promote Alex McGough, waive Cornell Armstrong |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/09/10/texans-promote-alex-mcgough-waive-cornell-armstrong/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> McGough was waived by Houston on October 16, and was re-signed to the team's practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=October 16, 2019 |title=Texans sign Chris Clark, place Seantrel Henderson on reserve list |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Texans-sign-Chris-Clark-Seantrel-Henderson-reserve-14538873.php |website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Texans on January 13, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 13, 2020 |title=Texans sign 10 players to reserve/future contracts |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-sign-10-players-to-reserve-future-contracts |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

McGough was waived on August 31, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=August 31, 2020 |title=Source: Texans cut third quarterback Alex McGough |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Source-Texans-cut-third-quarterback-Alex-McGough-15527539.php |access-date=August 31, 2020 |website=Houston Chronicle |language=en-US}}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on September 14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2020 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (9/14) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-9-14 |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> McGough was released by the Texans on October 12.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2020 |title=Houston Texans Transactions (10–12–20) |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-10-12-20 |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
On December 9, 2020, McGough was signed to the Seattle Seahawks' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=December 9, 2020 |title=Seahawks Sign Alex McGough To Practice Squad; Rashaad Penny & Quinton Dunbar Return To Practice |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-alex-mcgough-to-practice-squad-rashaad-penny-quinton-dunbar-return |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> On January 11, 2021, McGough signed a reserve/futures contract with the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=January 11, 2021 |title=Seahawks Sign 12 to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-12-to-reserve-future-contracts |access-date=February 17, 2021 |website=Seahawks.com |archive-date=January 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210128064808/https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-12-to-reserve-future-contracts |url-status=dead }}</ref> McGough was waived by Seattle on August 23.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=August 23, 2021 |title=Seahawks Place Two On Injured Reserve, Waive Two To Reduce Roster To 80 |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-place-two-on-injured-reserve-waive-two-to-reduce-roster-to-80 |access-date=May 26, 2023 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

===Birmingham Stallions (first stint)===
McGough was selected by the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL) with the sixth pick of the first round of the [[2022 USFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Duncan |first=Jordan |date=February 23, 2022 |title=Wednesday Round-Up: Former Seahawks QB Alex McGough Selected In USFL Draft |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/wednesday-round-up-former-seahawks-qb-alex-mcgough-selected-in-usfl-draft |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> He suffered an ankle injury,<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1516637205938065410 |user=USFLStallions |title=Tuesday Practice Report |date=April 20, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref> and was transferred to the inactive roster on April 22, 2022.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1517399866980274176 |user=USFLStallions |title=Transferred to inactive roster |date=April 22, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1517421291011149824 |user=USFLStallions |title=Game status report |date=April 22, 2022 |access-date=April 23, 2022}}</ref> He was moved back to the active roster on May 6.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1522476526666543104 |user=USFLStallions |title=Roster Updates |date=May 6, 2022 |access-date=May 6, 2022}}</ref> During the [[2022 USFL championship game]], McGough replaced an injured [[J'Mar Smith]], throwing for seven completions on 10 attempts for 77 yards, and a touchdown, helping the Stallions earn their first [[USFL championship game|USFL championship]].

McGough entered the [[2023 Birmingham Stallions season|2023 season]] as Smith's backup but was thrust back into the starting role when Smith suffered a season-ending injury in the Stallions' first game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2023 |title=Stallions QB J'Mar Smith out for season, Alex McGough takes starting role |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/usfl/stallions-qb-jmar-smith-out-for-season-alex-mcgough-new-starter |access-date=January 10, 2024 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He would go on to earn USFL MVP honors<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2023 |title=Birmingham Stallions QB Alex McGough named USFL MVP |url=https://www.theusfl.com/the-usfl/birmingham-stallions-qb-alex-mcgough-named-2023-usfl-most-valuable-player |access-date=January 10, 2024 |website=Fox Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> and lead the Stallions to their second consecutive [[2023 USFL championship game|USFL championship]].

McGough was released from his contract with the Stallions on July 18, 2023, to sign with an NFL team.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLStallions |title=Contract Terminated / Signing with NFL Team |number=1681438107290472449 |date=July 18, 2023 |access-date=July 19, 2023}}</ref>

'''Alex Light''' (born May 2, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[Tackle (gridiron football position)|offensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond Spiders]], and was signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2018. He also played for the [[Dallas Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Light [[letterman sports|lettered]] in football and basketball at [[Salem High School (Salem, Virginia)|Salem High School]]. Light was a two time all-state football player. He committed to [[Richmond Spiders football|Richmond]] over an offer from [[VMI Keydets football|VMI]].<ref name ="High School">{{citation |url= https://roanoke.com/sports/high_schools/article_0c24f17d-51b7-5fd4-9333-717507ffff89.html| title= Alex Light shocked to be on Green Bay Packers roster|work= Roanoke Times}}</ref>

==College career==

==Professional career==

'''William Alexander Green''' (born November 3, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana Hoosiers]].

==Early life==
Green attended [[Glenbard West High School]], where he was a two-way player at [[running back]] and [[defensive back]].

He accepted a football scholarship from [[Indiana University Bloomington]]. As a freshman, he was a backup [[running back]], registering 17 carries for 32 yards.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/indiana/1983.html |title=1983 Indiana Hoosiers Stats |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> As a sophomore, he was a backup behind [[Bobby Howard (running back)|Bobby Howard]], posting 68 carries for 168 yards, one [[touchdown]], 24 receptions for 189 yards and 18 kickoff returns for 311 yards.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/indiana/1984.html |title=1984 Indiana Hoosiers Stats | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

As a junior, he was moved to [[cornerback]] and was named a starter, finishing with one interception.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1985-07-28-8502190726-story.html |title=Illini, NU Make Key Switches |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1985-09-07-8502280688-story.html |title=Hoosiers Capsule |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, he was the starter at [[free safety]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1986-04-16-8601270749-story.html |title=NU Worries Arrive Early And Often |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He led the team with 5 interceptions (one returned for a [[touchdown]]) and received second-team [[Big Ten Conference|All-Big Ten]] honors.<ref name=AP>{{cite news|title=Harbaugh heads All-Big Ten team|newspaper=The Michigan Daily|date=November 26, 1986|page=8|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2706&dat=19861126&id=1A5KAAAAIBAJ&sjid=vx4NAAAAIBAJ&pg=1069,3998533| access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Green was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] after the [[1987 NFL draft]]. He was waived on August 31.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/09/01/sports/transactions-606387.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=September 1987 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

After the [[NFLPA]] strike was declared on the third week of the [[1987 NFL season|1987 season]], those contests were canceled (reducing the 16 game season to 15) and the [[NFL]] decided that the games would be played with replacement players. He was re-signed to be a part of the Dallas replacement team that was given the mock name "Rhinestone Cowboys" by the media.<ref>{{cite news|title=Who's playing today and for whom|newspaper=Lakeland Ledger|date=October 4, 1987}}</ref> He started 3 games at [[free safety]]. He had one interception against the [[New York Jets]]. He was released on October 26, at the end of the strike.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/10/27/sports/transactions-111087.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=October 27, 1987 | access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Green is the General Counsel for [[CareerBuilder.com]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.superlawyers.com/illinois/article/intercepted/32622137-1762-417b-bd82-24d14542a60c.html | title=CareerBuilder's Alex Green started in the NFL before redirecting to the law | access-date=April 21, 2018}}</ref>
Green’s favorite child is his only son, Joseph.

'''Alexander Leatherwood''' (born January 5, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], where he was two-time [[College Football Playoff National Championship|CFP national champion]] and the winner of the [[Outland Trophy|Outland]] and [[Jacobs Blocking Trophy|Jacobs Blocking]] trophies in 2020. Leatherwood was selected by the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] in the first round of the [[2021 NFL draft]], but was released after his rookie season.

==Early life==
Leatherwood was born on January 5, 1999, and grew up in [[Pensacola, Florida]], where he attended [[Booker T. Washington High School (Pensacola, Florida)|Booker T. Washington High School]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Houston |first=Bryce |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Alex Leatherwood: 3 things to know about the Alabama football offensive lineman |work=[[Montgomery Advertiser]] |url=https://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/2019/09/17/alex-leatherwood-alabama-football-roster-season-schedule-rankings/2276847001/ |access-date=November 7, 2019}}</ref> He was named first-team All-Area by the ''[[Pensacola News Journal]]'' as a junior and senior.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 1, 2017 |title=University of Alabama football class of 2017 |url=https://www.wbrc.com/story/34404593/university-of-alabama-football-class-of-2017/ |access-date=November 7, 2019 |website=WBRC.com}}</ref> As a senior, he was named a first-team [[All-American]] by ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' and named to the second-team by ''[[USA Today]]'' and played in the [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|All-America Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adame |first=Tony |date=January 8, 2018 |title=Leatherwood steps up for Alabama in title game |url=https://www.pnj.com/story/sports/college/alabama/2018/01/08/washingtons-leatherwood-delivers-clutch-alabama/1015809001/ |access-date=November 7, 2019 |website=[[Pensacola News Journal]]}}</ref> Leatherwood was rated a consensus five-star and top 10 recruit for his class and committed to play [[college football]] at the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|University of Alabama]] during his junior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sinor |first=Wesley |date=January 13, 2019 |title=Pensacola OT Alex Leatherwood is Alabama's 3rd commitment in 2 days |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2015/06/pensacola_ot_alex_leatherwood.html |access-date=November 7, 2019 |website=[[AL.com]]}}</ref>

(offensive lineman)|Jonah Williams]] was injured in the third quarter.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rill |first=Jake |date=January 8, 2018 |title=Alabama LT Jonah Williams exits with injury, goes to medical tent |work=[[Springfield News-Sun]] |url=https://www.springfieldnewssun.com/sports/college/alabama-jonah-williams-exits-with-injury-goes-medical-tent/fPhKTJbaJeyK7gbpN3CFxL/ |access-date=November 7, '''Alex M. Bars''' (born September 8, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and was signed as an undrafted free agent by the [[Chicago Bears]] following the [[2019 NFL draft]].

==College career==
Bars was a member of the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] for five seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2018 |title=Alex Bars |url=https://und.com/roster/alex-bars/ |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Notre Dame Fighting Irish - Official Athletics Website |language=en-US}}</ref> He spent his freshman year on the [[scout team]] before playing in six games with two starts as a sophomore. He started all 12 of Notre Dame's games at [[right tackle]] as a junior and all 13 games of his senior year at [[left guard]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farmer |first=Douglas |date=June 3, 2018 |title=Notre Dame 99-to-2: No. 71 Alex Bars, left guard and captain |url=https://irish.nbcsports.com/2018/06/03/notre-dame-99-to-2-no-71-alex-bars-left-guard-and-captain/ |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=[[NBCSports.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McJunkin |first=Connor |date=July 3, 2018 |title=Notre Dame Football: Sporting News Names Alex Bars Preseason All-American |url=https://slapthesign.com/2018/07/03/notre-dame-football-bars-preseason-american/ |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=SlapTheSign.com |publisher=[[FanSided]]}}</ref> Bars returned as a graduate student for a fifth season of [[NCAA]] eligibility and was named a preseason [[All-American]] by the ''[[Sporting News]]'', but tore his MCL and ACL five games into the season against Stanford.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prister |first=Tim |date=February 7, 2019 |title=Four Months After Knee Surgery, Alex Bars Presses On |url=https://247sports.com/college/notre-dame/Article/Four-Months-After-Knee-Surgery-Alex-Bars-Presses-On-128760516/ |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> Over the course of his college career, Bars played in 36 games with 32 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shepkowski |first=Nick |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Irish in the NFL: Alex Bars Finally Gets His Chance with Bears |url=https://fightingirishwire.usatoday.com/2019/10/15/former-irish-ol-alex-bars-finally-added-to-the-bears-53-man-roster/ |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=Fighting Irish Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On March 27, 2022, Bars signed a one-year contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=March 17, 2022 |title=Raiders sign Alex Bars |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2022/03/17/raiders-sign-alex-bars/ |access-date=March 20, 2022 |website=ProFootballTalk |language=en-US}}</ref> He was waived on August 30.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Raiders finalize initial 53-man roster for the 2022 season |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-finalize-initial-53-man-roster-2022-season-transactions-waive-release |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> On September 6, Bars was signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Damien |first=Levi |date=September 6, 2022 |title=Raiders re-sign G Alex Bars, WR Keelan Cole to practice squad |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2022/09/06/raiders-re-sign-g-alex-bars-wr-keelan-cole-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=September 6, 2022 |website=Raiders Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> Bars was elevated to the active roster on September 17, for the team's Week 2 game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=September 17, 2022 |title=NFL Transaction: Saturday 9/17 |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/nfl-transactions-saturday-9-17/ |access-date=September 17, 2022 |website=NFL Trade Rumors.com}}</ref> and on September 24, for the team's Week 3 game against the [[Tennessee Titans]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda |first=Nate |date=September 24, 2022 |title=NFL Transaction: Saturday 9/24 |url=https://nfltraderumors.co/nfl-transactions-saturday-9-24/ |access-date=September 24, 2022 |website=NFL Trade Rumors.com}}</ref> and on both cases was then reverted to the practice squad the next day. On October 1, the Raiders signed Bars to their active roster from the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2022 |title=Raiders sign G Alex Bars to active roster, Robey-Coleman and Guidry activated for Broncos matchup |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-guard-alex-bars-nfl-2022-transactions-week-4-broncos |access-date=October 1, 2022 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

On March 30, 2023, Bars re–signed with Las Vegas.<ref name="i650">{{cite web | title=Raiders re-sign G Alex Bars | website=Las Vegas Raiders | date=2023-03-30 | url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-re-sign-guard-alex-bars-nfl-2023-free-agency-transactions | access-date=2024-12-25}}</ref> On August 29, Bars was released by the Raiders.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Raiders finalize initial 53-man roster for the 2023 season |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-finalize-initial-53-man-roster-2023-nfl-season-transactions-08292023 |access-date=2025-01-16 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>
