'''Alex Highsmith''' (born August 7, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Charlotte 49ers football|Charlotte 49ers]].

==Early life==
Highsmith grew up in [[Wilmington, North Carolina]], and attended [[Eugene Ashley High School]], where he played baseball, basketball and football.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wwaytv3.com/2020/04/24/pittsburgh-steelers-draft-ashley-high-school-standout-alex-highsmith-102nd-overall/|title=Pittsburgh Steelers draft Ashley High School standout Alex Highsmith 102nd overall|last=Barth|first=Tanner|date=April 24, 2020|website=WWAY TV|language=en-US|access-date=April 26, 2020}}</ref> He played middle linebacker and fullback and was named second-team All-Area and first-team All-Mideastern Conference as a senior. He was also named All-Area in baseball. Highsmith was lightly recruited by college programs and only received interest from [[Davidson Wildcats football|Davidson]] and [[Furman Paladins football|Furman]] before being offered a spot on [[UNC Charlotte]]'s team as a walk on.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/charlotte-edge-rusher-alex-highsmith-prove/|title=Charlotte edge rusher Alex Highsmith still proving people wrong|first=Andrew|last=DiCecco|website=ProFootballNetwork.com|date=February 26, 2020|access-date=March 25, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Highsmith joined the [[Charlotte 49ers football|Charlotte 49ers]] as a walk-on and [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fuller |first=Jackson |date=December 5, 2016 |title=Highsmith keeps making strides at Charlotte |url=https://www.starnewsonline.com/sports/20161205/highsmith-keeps-making-strides-at-charlotte |access-date=March 25, 2020 |website=[[Star-News]]}}</ref> As a redshirt freshman, he played in all 12 of the 49ers games and finished the season with 17 tackles and a sack. Highsmith was a key member of Charlotte's defensive line rotation during his redshirt sophomore season and finished the year with 33 tackles with 5.0 tackles for loss, 2.0 sacks and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |first=David |date=August 13, 2019 |title=Alex Highsmith walked on to the Charlotte 49ers. Now he's a star. Is the NFL next? |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article233783377.html |access-date=March 25, 2020 |website=[[The News & Observer]]}}</ref> He was named a starter at defensive end as a redshirt junior and was named first-team All-[[Conference USA]] after setting a school record with 17.5 tackles for loss along with 60 total tackles, three sacks and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wect.com/2018/12/18/former-ashley-football-standout-goes-walk-starter-charlotte-ers/|title=Former Ashley football standout goes from walk on to starter for the Charlotte 49ers|website=[[WECT|WECT.com]]|date=December 17, 2018|access-date=March 25, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite ===2020===
Highsmith was selected by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the third round, 102nd overall, of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Steelers select Highsmith in the third round |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-select-highsmith-in-the-third-round?campaign=sf:fanshare:facebook |access-date=April 26, 2020 |website=Steelers.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In week 8 against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Highsmith recorded his first career interception off a pass thrown by [[Lamar Jackson]] during the 28–24 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens - November 1st, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011010rav.htm |access-date=November 4, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
In week 9 against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Highsmith recorded his first career sack on [[Garrett Gilbert]] during the 24–19 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Dallas Cowboys - November 8th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011080dal.htm |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
In week 13 against the [[Washington Football Team]], Highsmith made his starting debut. In it, he recorded five tackles in the Steelers first loss of the season. Highsmith finished  the remaining four games as the Steelers' starter, recording 23 more tackles as well as one sack that he recorded during their season finale against the [[Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns - January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030cle.htm |access-date=January 3, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Highsmith 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HighAl02/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2021===
[[File:Alex Highsmith (51654044521) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Highsmith during a game against the Cleveland Browns in 2021]]
In week 17, against the Browns, Highsmith had two sacks in the 26–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers - January 3rd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201030pit.htm |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2021 season, he had six sacks, 74 total tackles (46 solo), and one forced fumble in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Highsmith 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HighAl02/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He had one sack in the Steelers' Wild Card Round loss to the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Pittsburgh Steelers at Kansas City Chiefs - January 16th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201160kan.htm |access-date=May 17, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2022===
In the regular season opener, Highsmith had three sacks and a forced fumble in the 23–20 overtime victory over the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals - September 11th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209110cin.htm |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In week 10, Highsmith had five tackles, two sacks, a tackle for loss and a forced fumble in a 20–10 win over the [[New Orleans Saints]], earning [[American Football Conference]] (AFC) Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=November 16, 2022 |title=Vikings WR Justin Jefferson, Colts RB Jonathan Taylor lead Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-10-justin-jefferson-jonathan-taylor |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He closed out the 2022 regular season with 2.5 sacks in a 28–14 win over the Browns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers - January 8th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301080pit.htm |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

He finished the 2022 season with 63 tackles, a team high 14.5 sacks, and league-leading five forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Highsmith 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HighAl02/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Pittsburgh Steelers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/2022.htm |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/leaders.htm |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2023===
On July 19, 2023, Highsmith signed a four-year, $68 million contract extension with the Steelers. The contract includes $27.74 million guaranteed and a signing bonus of $16 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Baca |first=Michael |date=July 19, 2023 |title=Alex Highsmith, Steelers agree to terms on four-year, $68 million extension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/alex-highsmith-steelers-agree-to-terms-on-four-year-68-million-extension |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>
During week 2 of the 2023 season against the Browns, Highsmith intercepted the first pass from Browns quarterback [[Deshaun Watson]] and returned it 30 yards for his first NFL touchdown. He also recorded seven tackles and a forced fumble on Watson, which was recovered by Steelers teammate [[T. J. Watt]] for what eventually became the game-winning touchdown as the Steelers held on to win, 26–22. For his performance, Highsmith was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=September 20, 2023 |title=Alex Highsmith named the AFC defensive player of the week |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/alex-highsmith-named-the-afc-defensive-player-of-the-week |access-date=September 20, 2023 |website=NBCSports.com}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he finished with seven sacks, 57 tackles, two interceptions, three passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Highsmith 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HighAl02/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=December 26, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He had a sack in the Steelers' Wild Card Round loss to the Bills.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Pittsburgh Steelers at Buffalo Bills - January 15th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401150buf.htm |access-date=May 17, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2024===
In the 2024 season, Highsmith had six sacks, 45 tackles, and two passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Highsmith 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HighAl02/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=March 9, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He had a sack in the Steelers' Wild Card Round loss to the Ravens.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - Pittsburgh Steelers at Baltimore Ravens - January 11th, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202501110rav.htm |access-date=May 17, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2025===
In Week 9, Highsmith recorded four tackles, three tackles for loss, two sacks, and a forced fumble in a 27–20 win over the [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He was named AFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ravens QB Lamar Jackson, Bears TE Colston Loveland highlight Players of the Week|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2025-week-9-lamar-jackson-colston-loveland|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=November 5, 2025}}</ref> <ref>{{Cite web |last=Fitzgerald |first=Joe |date=January 15, 2026 |title=DeMeco Ryans Gives Huge Praise to Steelers Defender |url=https://steelersnow.com/demeco-ryans-gives-huge-praise-to-steelers-defender-after-wild-card-clash-they-dont-talk-about-you-enough/ |access-date=January 16, 2026 |website=Steelers Now |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished with a team high 9.5 sacks for the 2025 season to go with 50 total tackles (36 solo) and three passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 Pittsburgh Steelers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/pit/2025.htm |access-date=May 14, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Highsmith is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 25, 2020 |title=Walk-On Charlotte LB Selected In The 3rd Round of NFL Draft – Credits His Christian Faith |url=https://www.charlottestories.com/walk-on-charlotte-lb-selected-in-the-3rd-round-of-nfl-draft-credits-his-christian-faith/ |access-date=January 5, 2022 |website=Charlotte Stories}}</ref>

In 2023, Highsmith married Alyssa Ungrady, who competed in track and field for Charlotte.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |date=September 28, 2022 |title=Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith leads NFL in sacks with 'foundation in Christ' |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2022/09/28/steelers-alex-highsmith-sacks-foundation-christ/ |access-date=September 29, 2022 |website=Sports Spectrum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alyssa Ungrady - Track & Field |url=https://charlotte49ers.com/sports/track-and-field/roster/alyssa-ungrady/6541 |access-date=May 10, 2026 |website=Charlotte Athletics}}</ref>

Highsmith’s devotion to community service in the Pittsburgh, Wilmington and Charlotte areas has earned him recognition as the Pittsburgh Steelers’ nominee for the [[Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year|Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award]] in 2025. Through his foundation, the [https://www.alexhighsmithfamilyfoundation.org/ Alex Highsmith Family Foundation], he is focus on empowering the next generation through programs that focus Physical Fitness, Nutrition, Athletic Preparation, Family Involvement, Academic Success, and Emotional and Social Support.  Starting in 2021, his foundation has hosted annual youth football camps and fundraisers to raise funds to provide kids free essentials such as backpacks, haircuts, hygiene kits, books, and meals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=December 4, 2025 |title=Highsmith is Steelers Club Winner for 2025 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/highsmith-is-steelers-club-winner-for-2025-walter-payton-nfl-man-of-the-year-award |access-date=January 16, 2026 |website=www.steelers.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Perrine |first=Shannon |date=December 15, 2025 |title=Steelers linebacker Alex Highsmith leans on faith while running foundation, giving back to youth |url=https://www.wtae.com/article/alex-highsmith-faith-wife-walter-payton/69732246 |access-date=January 16, 2026 |website=WTAE |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alex Thomas Kessman''' (born January 2, 1998) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] for the [[New York Jets]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in 2021. He also played in the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] for the [[Memphis Showboats]] in 2023. He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]]

==College career==
He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. He set the NCAA record for most accurate placekicker in history from 50+ yards going 12 of 18 from that distance. 

In October 2019, Kessman was named ACC Specialist of the Week after making four field goals during the game against [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]].<ref name=specialist>{{cite news|title=Pitt's Alex Kessman Named ACC Specialist of the Week|url= https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2019/10/28/football-pitts-kessman-named-acc-specialist-of-the-week|access-date=19 November 2024|publisher=Pittsburgh Panthers|date=28 October 2019}}</ref>

In 2020, in a game against Boston College, Kessman kicked a 58-yard field goal which tied the game and sent it into overtime.<ref name="Scabilloni"/> At the time, the 58-yard goal was the longest field goal in [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Panthers]] history.<ref name="Scabilloni">{{cite news |last1=Scabilloni |first1=Matt |title=Watch: Pitt Kicker Makes Program History |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/football/watch-pitt-panthers-kicker-ben-sauls-makes-program-history-field-goal |access-date=19 November 2024 |publisher=Sports Illustrated |date=October 12, 2024}}</ref> In 2024, [[Ben Sauls]] tied Kessman's record.<ref name="Scabilloni"/>

In 2021, Kessman received second-team All-ACC honors and was a semifinalist for the [[Lou Groza Award]].<ref name=Calvaruso>{{cite news| last1=Calvaruso |first1=Tyler |title=4 things to know about Jets kicker Alex Kessman |url= https://jetswire.usatoday.com/lists/new-york-jets-kicker-alex-kessman-things-to-know-matt-ammendola/ |access-date=19 November 2024 |publisher=USA Today|date=November 24, 2021}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On May 2, 2021, Kessman signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pittsburghsportsnow.com/2021/05/02/pitt-kicker-alex-kessman-signs-with-los-angeles-chargers-as-udfa/|title=Pitt Kicker Alex Kessman Signs with Los Angeles Chargers as UDFA|date=2 May 2021}}</ref> However, Kessman was released by the Chargers prior to the start of the season on August 16, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/release-michael-bandy-lachlan-edwards-alex-kessman|title = Chargers Release Three Players}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
On November 23, 2021, Kessman was signed to the practice squad of the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-alex-kessman-to-practice-squad|title=Jets Sign K Alex Kessman to Practice Squad}}</ref> On December 4, the Jets released incumbent kicker [[Matt Ammendola]] and signed Kessman to the active roster.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-alex-kessman-to-active-roster-release-k-matt-ammendola|title=Jets Sign K Alex Kessman to Active Roster, Release K Matt Ammendola|website=[[New York Jets]]|access-date=2021-12-05|archive-date=2021-12-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205003508/https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-alex-kessman-to-active-roster-release-k-matt-ammendola|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his one game with the Jets, which was also his NFL debut, Kessman missed both of his extra point attempts and the Jets lost to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] by a score of 33–18. He was cut by the team the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alex-kessman-time-in-big-apple-ends/|title=Alex Kessman: Time in Big Apple ends|website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On December 22, 2021, Kessman was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-place-zane-gonzalez-on-injured-reserve|title=Panthers place Zane Gonzalez on injured reserve|website=Panthers.com|date=December 22, 2021}}</ref> He was released on December 27.

On January 28, 2023, Kessman signed with the [[Memphis Showboats (2022)|Memphis Showboats]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]] (USFL).<ref>{{cite tweet |user=USFLShowboats |title=Free Agent Signing |number= 1619336788098822145 |date=January 28, 2023 |access-date=January 28, 2023}}</ref> He was removed from the roster on February 15, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Memphis Showboats Roster |url=https://www.theufl.com/teams/memphis/roster |access-date=2024-02-15 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alexander Forsyth''' (born February 13, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon Ducks]].

==Early life==
Forsyth was born on February 13, 1999, in [[West Linn, Oregon|West Linn]], [[Oregon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2023 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410190932/https://cdn.theathletic.com/app/uploads/2023/04/10111751/TheBeast_NFL_Draft_Guide-1.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 10, 2023 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-07-06 |website=[[The Athletic]] |pages=154}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite magazine |date=July 13, 2022 |title=NFL Draft Profile: Alex Forsyth, Offensive Lineman, Oregon Ducks |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/draft/news/alexforsyth |access-date=2024-07-06 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He played football at [[West Linn High School]], where he was named first-team all-state as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] and [[Senior (education)|senior]].<ref name="auto" /> A three-star recruit, Forsyth committed to play [[college football]] at [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]].<ref name="auto" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Martini, Pete |date=January 13, 2017 |title=In-state recruit Alex Forsyth's commitment to Oregon Ducks has never wavered |url=https://www.statesmanjournal.com/story/sports/blogs/martini/2017/01/14/-state-recruit-alex-forsyths-commitment-oregon-ducks-has-never-wavered/96580488/ |access-date=2024-07-06 |work=[[Statesman Journal]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Forsyth [[Redshirt (sports)|redshirted]] his first year at Oregon in 2017.<ref name="auto" /> He appeared in five games in both of the following seasons, seeing action at [[right guard]], [[right tackle]] and [[left guard]].<ref name="auto1">{{Cite magazine |last=Torres, Max |date=July 23, 2022 |title=Alex Forsyth Named to Rimington Trophy Watch List for Nation's Best Center |url=https://www.si.com/college/oregon/football/oregon-footballs-alex-forsyth-named-to-rimington-trophy-watch-list-for-nations-best-center |access-date=2024-07-06 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He became a full-time starter in 2020, starting at [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] all seven games in the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]-shortened season.<ref name="auto1" /> He led the offense in snaps and only allowed one [[Quarterback sack|sack]], while being named second-team all-conference.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thorburn, Ryan |date=July 23, 2021 |title=Oregon Ducks center Alex Forsyth on Rimington Trophy watch list |url=https://www.registerguard.com/story/sports/college/football/2021/07/23/oregon-ducks-center-alex-forsyth-rimington-trophy-watch-list/8064315002/ |access-date=2024-07-06 |work=[[The Register-Guard]]}}</ref>

In 2021, Forsyth appeared in 10 of 14 games, starting nine at center while earning second-team all-conference honors again.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sheehan, Patrick |date=April 23, 2023 |title=Alex Forsyth 2023 NFL Draft Profile |url=https://www.yardbarker.com/college_football/articles/alex_forsyth_2023_nfl_draft_profile/s1_17198_38730326 |access-date=2024-07-06 |website=[[Yardbarker]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Call, Jeff |date=December 7, 2021 |title=Kyle Whittingham, Devin Lloyd and Junior Tafuna highlight Utah's Pac-12 award recipients |url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2021/12/7/22822829/utah-football-who-earned-all-pac-12-honors-kyle-whittingham-devin-lloyd-cam-rising-junior-tafuna |access-date=2024-07-06 |work=[[Deseret News]]}}</ref> After being given an extra year of eligibility due to the COVID-19 pandemic, he opted to return to Oregon in 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Neel, Zachary |date=November 24, 2021 |title=Alex Forsyth says he is returning to the Ducks next season |url=https://duckswire.usatoday.com/2021/11/24/report-alex-forsyth-says-he-is-returning-to-the-ducks-next-season/ |access-date=2024-07-06 |work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref> In his final year, he rated as the second-best pass blocking center nationally according to PFF's rankings, and was named a second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] selection.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2023 |title=31 former Pac-12 stars invited to 2023 NFL Combine |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2023/2/24/31-former-pac-12-stars-invited-2023-nfl-combine.aspx |access-date=2024-07-06 |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Crepea, James |date=December 9, 2022 |title=Oregon's Alex Forsyth named second team FWAA All-American |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/2022/12/oregons-alex-forsyth-named-second-team-fwaa-all-american.html |access-date=2024-07-06 |work=[[The Oregonian]]}}</ref>

'''Alex Andrzej Palczewski''' ({{IPAc-en|p|ɑː|l|ˈ|tʃ|ɛ|v|s|k|i}} {{respell|pahl|CHEV|skee}};<ref name=":1">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=neVbIN3rQv4 |title=Spotlighting Illinois' Alex Palczewski {{!}} Big Ten Football {{!}} The Journey |date=2022-11-01 |last=Big Ten Network |access-date=2024-09-27 |via=YouTube}}</ref> born August 3, 1999), nicknamed "'''Palcho'''",<ref name=":1" /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Palczewski played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Alex Palczewski |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4240551/alex-palczewski |website=ESPN |access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> where he was named a college football All-American for the 2022 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Three Illini named AFCA All-Americans |url=https://www.theintelligencer.com/sports/article/Three-Illini-named-AFCA-All-Americans-17656212.php |website=The Edwardsville Intellingencer |access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Bement |first1=Brice |title=Witherspoon, Palczewski and Brown named AFCA All-Americans |url=https://www.wcia.com/sports/witherspoon-palczewski-and-brown-named-afca-all-americans/ |website=WCIA.com |access-date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> He was signed by the Broncos as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2023.

== Early life ==
Palczewski was born in [[Mount Prospect, Illinois]] to Andrzej and Bozena Palczewski, both immigrants from [[Polish People's Republic|communist Poland]] who moved to the [[United States]] in the mid-1980s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ryan |first=Shannon |date=September 6, 2019 |title='I'm Polish and super proud of it': Illinois offensive tackle Alex Palczewski inherited his blue-collar work ethic from his immigrant parents |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-illinois-alex-palczewski-polish-20190906-2vcjwbzxljdxtdlw4ii3c4gm2y-story.html |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=Chicago Tribune}}</ref> His father worked as a carpenter and his mother worked as a nurse.<ref name=":0" /> Palczewski grew up speaking Polish, and was still learning English pronunciations through the third grade.<ref name=":0" /> Before football, he played [[Association football|soccer]] as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalie]].<ref name=":0" /> Palczewski competed in amateur wrestling throughout the course of his time in high school. He also spent two years each in [[water polo]] and [[track and field]].<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski">[https://fightingillini.com/sports/football/roster/alex-palczewski/12946 "Fighting Illini"] Profile. Retrieved November 17, 2024.</ref> 
In his junior year at Prospect, Palczewski received his first scholarship offer made by the [[VMI Keydets football|Virginia Military Institute]]. Rated a three-star athlete, Palczewski received interest from [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]], [[NC State Wolfpack football|North Carolina State]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota]], [[Michigan State Spartans football|Michigan State]] and [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana]]. He received offers from [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]], [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]] and Illinois.<ref name="Prospect OT A. Palczewski">[https://247sports.com/recruitment/alex-palczewski-100586/recruitinterests/ "247Sports"] Recruitment Profile. Retrieved November 17, 2024.</ref>
Sports writers suggested Palczewski's recruitment potential might have been negatively effected by his absence from his junior season due to a neck injury including a [[Cervical fracture|fractured vertebrae]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Illinois Fighting Illini Football Recruiting">{{cite web |last=Vainisi |first=Jim |date=January 24, 2017 |title=Three-star OL Alex Palczewski commits to Illinois Football |url=https://www.thechampaignroom.com/2017/1/23/14367496/alex-palczewski-illinois-fighting-illini-football-recruiting-news-rumors-vanderbilt-syracuse |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=The Champaign Room |publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Alex Palczewski (52513802882) (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|Palczewski with the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]] in 2022]]
Choosing loyalty to his home state, Palczewski committed to Illinois.<ref name="Illinois Fighting Illini Football Recruiting"/> He began his first season in 2017. After missing the opening game, Palczewski joined [[Vederian Lowe]] and Larry Boyd in making college history as Illinois' first-ever [[Redshirt (college sports)|true freshmen]] starters on the offensive line. He played as a starting [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the last 11 games of the season.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/> In the 2018 season, Palczewski played as a starting right tackle for all 12 games. During his sophomore season, Palczewski was named to the All-Big Ten first team.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/> He continued in this role for his junior season in 2019, starting in all 13 games.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/> During the 2020 season as a senior, Palczewski played as starting right tackle for four games before missing the season's final four games due to injury. Despite this, he earned Big Ten third team honors.

During the 2021 season, Palczewski played seven games as a starting tackle and five games as a starting guard. After playing in all 12 games, he earned Big Ten third team honors. For his final senior season in 2022, he returned to his starting right tackle position and played in all 13 games. For his performances, Palczewski collected numerous All-American and Big Ten honors including being named to first, second and third teams. He also served as [[team captain]] for the season.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/> Palczewski graduated with a [[bachelor's degree]] in [[kinesiology]] in 2021.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/>

On February 21, 2023, Palczewski was drafted 68th overall by the [[2023 New Orleans Breakers season|New Orleans Breakers]] in the [[2023 USFL draft]], though he never signed with them.<ref>{{Cite web |last=BigP |date=2023-02-21 |title=2023 USFL Draft recap: 80 players selected across 10 rounds - BigPaulSports |url=https://bigpaulsports.com/2023/02/2023-usfl-draft-recap-80-players-selected-across-10-rounds/ |access-date=2025-05-01 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Palczewski was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] as an undrafted free agent on May 12, 2023. He was placed on injured reserve on August 31, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign NT Mike Purcell, CB Fabian Moreau and T Quinn Bailey, place three players on injured reserve|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-nt-mike-purcell-cb-fabian-moreau-and-t-quinn-bailey-place-three-pla|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=August 31, 2023}}</ref> He was activated on January 6, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |date=January 6, 2024 |title=Broncos promote CB Art Green, activate T Alex Palczewksi from IR, elevate S Devon Key for Week 18 vs. Raiders |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-promote-cb-art-green-activate-t-alex-palczewksi-from-ir-elevate-s-devon- |access-date=August 14, 2024 |website=DenverBroncos.com}}</ref>

Palczewski made his first start in Week 3 of the [[2024 NFL season|2024 season]], taking over for an injured [[Mike McGlinchey (offensive lineman)|Mike McGlinchey]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Melendrez Stapleton |first=Arnie |date=2024-09-18 |title=Mike McGlinchey is on IR so Alex Palczewski is set for 1st NFL start after 65 starts at Illinois |url=https://apnews.com/article/denver-broncos-mcglinchey-3cfc8ed52756f5229fe83ddd8db122ad |access-date=2024-09-22 |work=AP News}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Weir |first=Susanna |date=2024-09-18 |title=Broncos Notebook: T Alex Palczewski set to make first NFL start |url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-notebook-t-alex-palczewski-set-to-make-first-nfl-start |access-date=2024-10-21 |website=Denver Broncos |language=}}</ref> It was reported on October 7, 2024, that Palczewski had suffered a high-ankle sprain during the Week 5 win over the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref name="e242">{{cite web |last=Kelberman |first=Zack |date=2024-10-07 |title=Report: Broncos RT Alex Palczewski Suffers High-Ankle Sprain |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/alex-palczewski-high-ankle-sprain-injury-update |access-date=2025-03-14 |website=Denver Broncos on SI}}</ref>

During the 2025 season, Broncos fans started to cheer every time Palczewski was reported as an eligible receiver when lining up as the jumbo set tight end for rushing plays.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klis |first=Mike |date=2025-10-03 |title=Meet Broncos Alex Palczewski |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/nfl/denver-broncos/mike-klis/denver-broncos-alex-palczewski/73-02af2225-f026-461f-b2f2-eb76ff62e8e5 |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=9news.com}}</ref> He primarily played as the backup right tackle until Week 7, when left guards [[Ben Powers (American football)|Ben Powers]] and [[Matt Peart]] were on injured reserve and Palczewski started at the position despite never having played it before.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=2025-10-16 |title=Alex Palczewski “ready for the challenge” of starting at left guard, Broncos LT Garett Bolles says |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2025/10/16/alex-palczewski-left-guard-broncos/ |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref> 

On March 5, 2026, the Broncos signed Palczewski to a two-year, $9.5 million contract extension instead of placing an RFA tender on him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Legwold |first=Jeff |date=2026-03-05 |title=The Broncos have agreed to terms on a two-year deal for T/G... |url=https://www.espn.com/contributor/jeff-legwold/05fbda3ec5be9 |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=ESPN |language=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=2026-03-05 |title=Broncos, OL Alex Palczewski agree to two-year, $9.5 million deal |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2026/03/05/broncos-sign-alex-palczewski-two-year-contract/ |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=The Denver Post |language=}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Palczewski has two brothers.<ref name=":0" /> Throughout his college and NFL careers, he has gone by the nickname "Palcho" due to his Polish surname being difficult for his teammates and coaches to pronounce.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> During his Illinois senior season in 2021 Palczewski co-presided over Lift for Life, a local charity group whose cause is to raise money and awareness for people battling rare diseases.<ref name="x538">{{Cite web |last=Boyd |first=Jason |date=2024-10-28 |title=Illinois' Alex Palczewski leads Lift for Life group to victory while raising money for good cause |url=https://thesouthern.com/sports/college/illini/illinois-alex-palczewski-leads-lift-for-life-group-to-victory-while-raising-money-for-good/article_d061c2d4-afab-59cf-b8bf-e469f107e997.html#2 |access-date=2024-12-06 |website=Southern Illinoisan}}</ref> Palczewski named [[Ivan Drago]] as his favorite athlete, acknowledging while Drago is fictional, he admired Drago's decision not to express himself through words but through his athletic talent and work ethic.<ref name="Illinois OL A. Palczewski"/>

'''Alex Cook''' (born May 21, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL). Cook played [[college football]] for the [[Washington Huskies football|Washington Huskies]] and was signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[New York Giants]] in {{NFL Year|2023}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Cook - Carolina Panthers Safety |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4243320/alex-cook |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
Alex Cook was born on May 21, 1999, in [[Sacramento, California]]. Cook attended [[Sheldon High School (California)|Sheldon High School]] in [[Elk Grove, California]], a suburb of Sacramento. He played both offense and defense for the Sheldon High School football team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Joe |date=February 1, 2017 |title=Alex Cook, Sheldon football, talks about signing national letter of intent with Washington |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/high-school/joe-davidson/article130063444.html |access-date=October 22, 2023 |website=[[The Sacramento Bee]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Rated as the 220th-best prospect in the nation, Cook chose to attend the [[University of Washington]] and play football there. In 2017, Cook [[redshirted]] and thus did not play the entire year. The next year, Cook played in twelve games and started one as a [[wide receiver]]. 
Cook changed his position during his redshirt sophomore year, becoming a defensive back and playing in all thirteen games for Washington. 
In 2020, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the season for Washington was shortened, and thus Cook only started three out of all four games.
Cook then started nine out of the eleven games he played in his redshirt senior year. Because of the shortened season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Cook was allowed to play one more season for Washington. In this season, Cook started in all thirteen games and was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] Second team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Cook |url=https://gohuskies.com/sports/football/roster/alex-cook/14195 |access-date=2024-07-08 |website=Washington Huskies}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On October 17, 2023, the [[Carolina Panthers]] signed Cook to their active roster off the Giants' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=October 17, 2023 |title=Panthers sign S Alex Cook off Giants practice squad |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/panthers-sign-s-alex-cook-off-giants-practice-squad |access-date=October 22, 2023 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

On August 27, 2024, Cook was waived by the Panthers and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers make moves to get to initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-moves-to-get-to-initial-53-man-roster|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nine players signed to practice squad|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/nine-players-signed-to-practice-squad|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> He was released on December 3.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rizzuti |first1=Anthony |title=Panthers announce flurry of practice-squad moves, including 4 additions |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/2024/12/03/panthers-practice-squad-emani-bailey-thomas-incoom-tj-luther-dominique-dafney/ |website=Panthers Wire |access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref>

===New York Giants (second stint)===

On January 22, 2025, Cook signed a reserve/future contract with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Wiltfong Jr. | first=Lester A.| title=Chicago Bears sign two more players to reserve/futures contracts | website=Windy City Gridiron|publisher=SB Nation | date=2025-01-23 | url=https://www.windycitygridiron.com/2025/1/23/24350102/chicago-bears-sign-two-more-players-to-reserve-futures-contracts-alex-cook-joshua-miles | access-date=2025-11-19}}</ref> He was waived on August 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chicago Bears announce roster moves|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/chicago-bears-announce-roster-moves-august-25-2025|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=August 25, 2025}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Stallions ===
On January 14, 2026, Cook was selected by the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Day Two of UFL Draft Introduces New Faces and Ignites the New Era of Spring Football |url=https://www.theufl.com/news/day-two-of-ufl-draft-introduces-new-faces-and-ignites-the-new-era-of-spring-football |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]] and was signed by the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2024. ==Early life== Johnson attended [[Loyola High School (Los Angeles)|Loyola High School]] in [[Los Angeles]], where he was a multi-sport athlete in [[high school football|football]], [[basketball]],{{cite web |last=Yancher |first=Owen |title=Alexander Johnson: TCL Student Signs with New York Giants |website=UCLA School of Education & Information Studies |url=https://seis.ucla.edu/alexander-johnson-tcl-student-signs-with-new-york-giants/ |date=June 15, 2024 |access-date=December 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524093924/https://seis.ucla.edu/web/20250524093924/https://seis.ucla.edu/alexander-johnson-tcl-student-signs-with-new-york-giants/ |archive-date=May 24, 2025}} and [[track and field]].{{cite web |title=Alex Johnson |website=Colts.com |url=https://www.colts.com/team/players-roster/alex-johnson/ |access-date=December 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814085453/https://www.colts.com/team/players-roster/alex-johnson/ |archive-date=August 14, 2025}} His scholarship offer to play football at [[Montana Grizzlies football|Montana]] was rescinded after a coaching change at the program, so he accepted a [[walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] offer at UCLA. ==College career== Johnson earned an undergraduate degree in [[political science]] and a master's degree in transformative coaching and leadership at [[UCLA]] while playing on the school's football team; originally a walk-on, he was offered a scholarship after his second season. He played in one game in 2018, all twelve games in 2019, six games in 2020 (the season that was shortened due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]), ten games in 2021, and all thirteen games in 2022. In 2023, he played in all thirteen games, starting in eight of them. His five [[interception]]s led the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. He recorded a [[fumble]] return [[touchdown]] against [[USC Trojans football|USC]] and a blocked [[punt (gridiron football)|punt]] against [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]]. He also intercepted a pass in UCLA's win against [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State]] in the [[2023 LA Bowl|LA Bowl]].{{cite web |title=Alex Johnson |website=UCLA Athletics |url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/football/roster/alex-johnson/12670 |access-date=December 25, 2024
